## Summary
- Fix CORS_ORIGINS environment variable parsing from JSON or comma-separated strings
- Add regex pattern for Vercel preview deployment URLs
- Update to pydantic v2 SettingsConfigDict syntax

## Root Cause
The CORS_ORIGINS environment variable was not being properly parsed from string format to a list, causing CORS preflight requests to fail.

## Changes
- `config.py`: Add `field_validator` to parse CORS_ORIGINS from JSON array or comma-separated string
- `main.py`: Add `allow_origin_regex` for Vercel preview deployments (`https://city-doodle-web-*.vercel.app`)

## Test plan
- [x] All unit tests pass
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Login works from production (city-doodle-web.vercel.app)

author: yuzefovich
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #162281 on behalf of @yuzefovich.
Backport 1/1 commits from #162460 on behalf of @yuzefovich.

----

A few months ago we fixed the propagation of some query-level metricsfrom routines. This required introducing a special `metadataForwarder` on the planner, and then we had to be careful to not use the wrong one when running plan inside the plan, so the field might be unset - until the plan is almost ready to be run. In production builds, the unset forwarder is ok - we simply drop some metadata. In test builds, we panic with an internal error.

We just saw a test case where - with the current setup - it's expected that this panic would occur. In particular, if we evaluate a routine during the physical planning, before the forwarder is set, we would run into the nil pointer. It's not easy to change things to set the proper forwarder earlier, so, instead, this commit simply sets the noop forwarder implementation as an expected exception - if we're still in the physical planning, we now simply drop metadata too. This shouldn't be that frequent (on a quick glance only frame bounds from window functions as well as VALUES clauses are affected).

Fixes: #161486.
Release note: None

----

Release justification: effectively test-only change.

author: yuzefovich
body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #162158 on behalf of @yuzefovich.

----

Increase the time we wait for the statement to be cancelled due to the statement timeout from 1 min to 3 min - the idea is that if we're blocked on something, then we'll now be able to see 1-2 min blockages (whereas previously it wasn't as clear whether the goroutine is running or is blocked since it's been in that state for less than 1 min).

Additionally, unskip one "expected" error that has been fixed in 25.4+.

Fixes: #161233.
Release note: None

----

Release justification: test-only change.

author: svaningelgem
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff), [changelog](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)) | dev | minor | `0.14.14` -> `0.15.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/ruff (ruff)</summary>

### [`v0.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0150)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/compare/0.14.14...0.15.0)

Released on 2026-02-03.

Check out the [blog post](https://astral.sh/blog/ruff-v0.15.0) for a migration
guide and overview of the changes!

##### Breaking changes

- Ruff now formats your code according to the 2026 style guide. See the formatter section below or in the blog post for a detailed list of changes.

- The linter now supports block suppression comments. For example, to suppress `N803` for all parameters in this function:

  ```python
  ```

### ruff: disable\[N803]

```
def foo(
    legacyArg1,
    legacyArg2,
    legacyArg3,
    legacyArg4,
): ...
```

### ruff: enable\[N803]

````
```

See the [documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/#block-level) for more details.
````

- The `ruff:alpine` Docker image is now based on Alpine 3.23 (up from 3.21).

- The `ruff:debian` and `ruff:debian-slim` Docker images are now based on Debian 13 "Trixie" instead of Debian 12 "Bookworm."

- Binaries for the `ppc64` (64-bit big-endian PowerPC) architecture are no longer included in our releases. It should still be possible to build Ruff manually for this platform, if needed.

- Ruff now resolves all `extend`ed configuration files before falling back on a default Python version.

##### Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

- [`blocking-http-call-httpx-in-async-function`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blocking-http-call-httpx-in-async-function)
  (`ASYNC212`)
- [`blocking-path-method-in-async-function`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blocking-path-method-in-async-function)
  (`ASYNC240`)
- [`blocking-input-in-async-function`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blocking-input-in-async-function)
  (`ASYNC250`)
- [`map-without-explicit-strict`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/map-without-explicit-strict)
  (`B912`)
- [`if-exp-instead-of-or-operator`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/if-exp-instead-of-or-operator)
  (`FURB110`)
- [`single-item-membership-test`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/single-item-membership-test)
  (`FURB171`)
- [`missing-maxsplit-arg`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/missing-maxsplit-arg) (`PLC0207`)
- [`unnecessary-lambda`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-lambda) (`PLW0108`)
- [`unnecessary-empty-iterable-within-deque-call`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-empty-iterable-within-deque-call)
  (`RUF037`)
- [`in-empty-collection`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/in-empty-collection) (`RUF060`)
- [`legacy-form-pytest-raises`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/legacy-form-pytest-raises)
  (`RUF061`)
- [`non-octal-permissions`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/non-octal-permissions) (`RUF064`)
- [`invalid-rule-code`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-rule-code) (`RUF102`)
- [`invalid-suppression-comment`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/invalid-suppression-comment)
  (`RUF103`)
- [`unmatched-suppression-comment`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unmatched-suppression-comment)
  (`RUF104`)
- [`replace-str-enum`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/replace-str-enum) (`UP042`)

The following behaviors have been stabilized:

- The `--output-format` flag is now respected when running Ruff in `--watch` mode, and the `full` output format is now used by default, matching the regular CLI output.
- [`builtin-attribute-shadowing`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/builtin-attribute-shadowing/) (`A003`) now detects the use of shadowed built-in names in additional contexts like decorators, default arguments, and other attribute definitions.
- [`duplicate-union-member`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/duplicate-union-member/) (`PYI016`) now considers `typing.Optional` when searching for duplicate union members.
- [`split-static-string`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/split-static-string/) (`SIM905`) now offers an autofix when the `maxsplit` argument is provided, even without a `sep` argument.
- [`dict-get-with-none-default`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/dict-get-with-none-default/) (`SIM910`) now applies to more types of key expressions.
- [`super-call-with-parameters`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/super-call-with-parameters/) (`UP008`) now has a safe fix when it will not delete comments.
- [`unnecessary-default-type-args`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unnecessary-default-type-args/) (`UP043`) now applies to stub (`.pyi`) files on Python versions before 3.13.

##### Formatter

This release introduces the new 2026 style guide, with the following changes:

- Lambda parameters are now kept on the same line and lambda bodies will be parenthesized to let
  them break across multiple lines ([#​21385](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21385))
- Parentheses around tuples of exceptions in `except` clauses will now be removed on Python 3.14 and
  later ([#​20768](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/20768))
- A single empty line is now permitted at the beginning of function bodies ([#​21110](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21110))
- Parentheses are avoided for long `as` captures in `match` statements ([#​21176](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21176))
- Extra spaces between escaped quotes and ending triple quotes can now be omitted ([#​17216](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/17216))
- Blank lines are now enforced before classes with decorators in stub files ([#​18888](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/18888))

##### Preview features

- Apply formatting to Markdown code blocks ([#​22470](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22470), [#​22990](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22990), [#​22996](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22996))

  See the [documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#markdown-code-formatting) for more details.

##### Bug fixes

- Fix suppression indentation matching ([#​22903](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22903))

##### Rule changes

- Customize where the `fix_title` sub-diagnostic appears ([#​23044](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/23044))
- \[`FastAPI`] Add sub-diagnostic explaining why a fix was unavailable (`FAST002`) ([#​22565](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22565))
- \[`flake8-annotations`] Don't suggest `NoReturn` for functions raising `NotImplementedError` (`ANN201`, `ANN202`, `ANN205`, `ANN206`) ([#​21311](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21311))
- \[`pyupgrade`] Make fix unsafe if it deletes comments (`UP017`) ([#​22873](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22873))

- \[`refurb`] Do not add `abc.ABC` if already present (`FURB180`) ([#​22234](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22234))
- \[`refurb`] Make fix unsafe if it deletes comments (`FURB110`) ([#​22768](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22768))
- \[`ruff`] Add sub-diagnostics with permissions (`RUF064`) ([#​22972](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22972))

The timezone toggle button added in #3119 used hardcoded light-mode colors. This replaces them with CSS custom properties from the sphinx_immaterial theme so the button adapts to dark mode.

body:
Github Issue: #148 

### Description

Workflow runs that produce a lot of images will generate a lot of harmony job metadata, meaning there will be a lot of text in the payload that gets passed between steps in the AWS Step Function. AWS enforces a 256 KB limit on the size of these messages, so it is important to cut down on their size where possible. This update passes only the harmony job information into the "Generate Image Metadata" lambda if sendToHarmony is true (i.e., the Harmony workflow path). This eliminates the need for the "Process Harmony Results" lambda, since its function will be performed inside "Generate Image Metadata" now.

### Overview of work done

* Refactored State Machine Definition (state_machine_definition.tpl) to go from check_harmony_job_status directly to generate_image_metadata on success, once all harmony jobs have completed. The "pass state" that used to come out of "process harmony results" now comes out of "check harmony job status". The "process harmony results" step has been eliminated
* The "check harmony job status" lambda has been updated to raise a HarmonyJobNoDataError under the same conditions as the "process harmony results" lambda used to.
* The "Generate Image Metadata" lambda now pulls down the file results from the harmony job status page if it detects that the payload it received is from a set of harmony job runs rather the opera hls treatment.

### Overview of verification done

* Since this is primarily a workflow update, testing will be performed with a deployment to SIT.

### Overview of integration done

* Tested the following data sets in the SIT venue:
    - OPERA HLS
    - PREFIRE COG
    - TEMPO NO2

* [X] Linted
* [x] Updated unit tests
* [x] Updated changelog
* [x] Integration testing

body:
The PG17 SETs are problematic mainly due to the `search_path` clearing. We run the schema dumps and loads within the same schema we are working in, so clearing the search_path messes with it.

EG when I load a table that has a trigger on it, the trigger itself wasn't specifying a schema on the tables it was calling, so this bombed out. The trigger itself should be explicit on the schema calling, but for `belt`'s perspective, we should be working within the confines of the schema anyways.

## Summary

Fixes test isolation failure causing flaky `TestKeychainStore_Concurrent*` tests.

- Root cause: Service name collisions when tests run with `-count=N` or in parallel
- Tests reused the same service name (`t.Name()`), causing "key already exists" errors from stale keychain data

## Changes

- Add nanosecond timestamp to `testServiceName()` for uniqueness across runs
- Clean up keychain BEFORE tests (not just after) to handle stale data from previous runs

## Testing

```
# Before fix: 6/20 failures
go test -run 'TestKeychainStore_Concurrent' ./crypto/... -count=5

# After fix: 40/40 pass
go test -run 'TestKeychainStore_Concurrent' ./crypto/... -count=10
```

Closes #182

## Summary

- Add `--json` flag for machine-readable output that agents can parse
- Add `require_interactive` check when user input is needed (prevents hanging when run non-interactively)
- Add 5-second timeouts to all `subprocess.run` calls in detector.py to prevent hangs
- Handle `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` exceptions gracefully

## Why

The retrofit command was designed for interactive CLI use, but AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) operate non-interactively. These changes make retrofit agent-native by:

1. **JSON output**: Agents can parse structured results instead of human-readable text
2. **Interactive detection**: Fails fast with a helpful message when user input would be needed
3. **Timeouts**: Prevents git commands from hanging indefinitely

Rebased from #96 which had merge conflicts.

author: omarshahine
body:
## Summary

- Migrate YNAB API token storage from plain text file to encrypted macOS Keychain
- Use `env/YNAB_API_TOKEN` service name, matching the YNAB MCP server wrapper pattern
- Add automatic migration for legacy file-based tokens
- Bump plugin version to 1.4.0

## Security Improvement

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Plain text file (`~/.config/credit-card-benefits/ynab-token`) | macOS Keychain (`env/YNAB_API_TOKEN`) |
| Protected by file permissions (600) | Encrypted at rest by macOS |
| Backed up in plain text by Time Machine | Protected by login keychain password |

## Changes

- `commands/ynab.md` - Token check, storage, retrieval, security docs
- `commands/configure.md` - Token storage, file locations table  
- `commands/sync.md` - Token retrieval, error handling
- `plugin.json` - Version bump 1.3.0 → 1.4.0

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `/credit-card-benefits:ynab setup` and verify token stored in Keychain
- [ ] Run `/credit-card-benefits:sync` and verify it retrieves token from Keychain
- [ ] Verify legacy file migration works (if old token file exists)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes how the YNAB token is stored/retrieved and adds Keychain interactions that could fail due to permissions, breaking setup or sync on affected machines.
> 
> **Overview**
> Migrates YNAB Personal Access Token handling from `~/.config/credit-card-benefits/ynab-token` to macOS Keychain under service `env/YNAB_API_TOKEN`, including verification steps and updated retrieval in `configure`, `ynab setup`, and `sync` flows.
> 
> Adds automatic migration: if a legacy token file exists, `ynab setup` attempts to import it into Keychain and removes the file on success (otherwise preserves it and continues for that session). Updates error messaging/docs and bumps plugin version to `1.4.0`.
>

feat(runtime): Implement Structured PERMIT Contract & Local Workflows

## Description

This PR implements the **Structured PERMIT Contract** (roadmap v1) and significantly improves the local development experience and CI robustness for the GlassOps Runtime.

### Key Changes

**Core Runtime**

- **Permit Contract**: New structured permit system with identity binding, policy validation, and contract generation
- **Absolute Path Handling**: `policy.go` now correctly handles absolute `GLASSOPS_CONFIG_PATH` values

**Developer Experience**

- Added `runtime:build` and `runtime:test` npm scripts
- VS Code launch configuration for debugging with `.env` support
- Comprehensive `.gitignore` for runtime artifacts

**CI/CD Improvements**

- Consolidated integration tests into `runtime-docker.yml`
- Fixed artifact upload for `.glassops/` directory
- Upgraded `docker/build-push-action` to v6
- Pinned `trivy-action@0.29.0` for security scanning
- Fixed Go module cache paths for all jobs
- Refactored tests to avoid emitting spurious CI warnings

**Documentation**

- Updated `packages/runtime/README.md` with architecture overview
- Generated AI documentation for runtime packages

## Test Plan

- [x] Local `go test ./...` passes
- [x] `runtime:build` produces valid binary
- [x] CI workflow runs without errors
- [x] Integration tests verify permit/contract artifact generation

## Breaking Changes

None - this is additive functionality.

This PR implements the standardized changes for LFXV2-872 to tie chart releases to app releases.

## Changes Made

### Chart.yaml Updates
- Reset version from `0.2.5` to `0.0.1` 
- Added explanatory comment about dynamic version replacement during chart build
- Updated `appVersion` to `"latest"` for consistency

### GitHub Workflow Updates  
- Updated `CHART_VERSION` calculation to use `github.ref_name` instead of reading from Chart.yaml
- Updated `helm-chart-oci-publisher` to newer version `@17e4144d7ba68f7c3e8c16eece5aed15fd7c2dc8`

## Related
- **Jira**: LFXV2-872 - Tie chart releases to app releases  
- **Pattern**: Standardized changes applied across all LFX v2 repositories

## Testing
The changes ensure that:
- Chart version is dynamically set to match the release tag during builds
- Chart builds use the updated publisher with latest features
- Version consistency between application and chart releases

### Motivation
- The document list should surface monetary values (Brutto/Netto/Steuer) and fall back to extracted metadata when model fields are missing.
- Document metadata must be editable from the UI via right-click/context menu to allow corrections and reprocessing.
- Sensitive payload fields should be redacted when showing raw metadata in the UI.

### Description
- Added a JSON formatter helper `def _format_json(value, *, redact_payload=False)` to pretty-print metadata and redact large/base64 fields.
- Introduced an editable metadata dialog (`meta_dialog`) with `ui.textarea` fields for `raw_payload_json`, `line_items_json` and `compliance_flags_json` and a `_save_meta` handler that updates `DocumentMeta` in the database via `get_session()` and `select(DocumentMeta)`.
- Added a context-menu entry `✏️ Metadaten` that opens the metadata dialog via the existing `_open_meta` UI handler and set `meta_state` to keep the current `doc_id` and values.

author: tigerroll
body:
## Overview

This pull request performs a major refactoring of the adapter layer in the Surfin Batch Framework. The primary goal is to eliminate direct dependencies on specific technologies (especially databases) from the framework's core layer. This significantly enhances system scalability, loose coupling, maintainability, and testability.

Key changes include consolidating general-purpose resource operation interfaces into the `pkg/batch/core/adapter` package and moving database-specific interfaces to `pkg/batch/adapter/database`. Additionally, GORM providers for each database type (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite) have been decoupled into individual Fx modules, allowing for more flexible integration via the DI container (Fx).

For strategies and further details regarding this refactoring, please refer to the newly added documentation: `docs/strategy/adapter_refactoring_strategy.md`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Reorganization of the Adapter Layer
* **New `pkg/batch/core/adapter/adapter.go`**: Defined general-purpose interfaces common to all resource types, such as `ResourceConnection`, `ResourceProvider`, and `ResourceConnectionResolver`. The existing `DBConnectionResolver` has been moved here and redefined as a generic resolver.
* **Decoupling the Core Layer**: Removed database-related interfaces (e.g., `DBConnectionResolver`) from `pkg/batch/core/application/port/interfaces.go` to ensure the core layer no longer depends on database-specific abstractions.
* **New `pkg/batch/adapter/database/interfaces.go`**: Defined database-specific interfaces (`DBExecutor`, `DBConnection`, `DBProvider`, `DBConnectionResolver`) that embed the general-purpose interfaces defined in `core/adapter`.

### 2. Decoupling GORM Database Providers
* **Provider Separation**: Removed concrete `DBProvider` implementations (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite) and related test helpers from `pkg/batch/adapter/database/gorm/provider.go`.
* **Database-Specific Modules**: Moved these implementations to their respective packages under `pkg/batch/adapter/database/gorm/{mysql,postgres,sqlite}/provider.go`.
* **Fx Integration**: Created new `module.go` files for each database type. Used `fx.Provide` and `fx.As(new(adapter.DBProvider))` to register each provider as a generic `adapter.DBProvider` within the Fx container.

### 3. DI Container (Fx) Adjustments and Dependency Updates
* **Updated Type References**: Replaced occurrences of `port.DBConnectionResolver` with the newly defined `adapter.DBConnectionResolver` throughout the framework, shifting dependencies to a more abstract layer.
* **Simplified Selection Logic**: In `example/weather/cmd/weather/main.go`, the DB provider selection logic was simplified to directly import and use the specific Fx modules. This transitions from dynamic environment-based selection to explicit build-time provider inclusion.
* **Refined Module Provision**: Updated the return type of `NewDefaultDBConnectionResolver` in `example/weather/internal/app/module.go` to `adapter.DBConnectionResolver` and adjusted Fx provision accordingly.

### 4. Migration of Test Helper Functions
* Moved test-specific functions like `GetConnectionStringForTest` and `GetDialectorForTest` from the provider code into the relevant test packages. This improves the independence and cohesion of the test code.

### 5. New Documentation
* Added `docs/strategy/adapter_refactoring_strategy.md`, which provides a detailed explanation of the background, objectives, new design philosophy, and future plans for this refactoring.

### 6. Miscellaneous
* Improved the comparison logic for `ExecutionContext` in `test/pkg/batch/engine/step/partition/partition_step_test.go` to better handle non-deterministic keys (e.g., `start`).

author: cdemeke
body:
## Summary
Addresses Apple App Store review feedback requiring citations for medical/health information (guideline 1.4.1).

## Apple's Feedback
> The app includes medical information but does not include citations for the medical information. Specifically, the app provides health or medical recommendations, references, and diagnoses without citations.

## Changes

### New MedicalInformationView
A dedicated view with comprehensive medical information citations from reputable sources:
- American Diabetes Association
- Diabetes UK  
- JDRF
- Mayo Clinic
- NIH/PubMed
- Pump manufacturers (Insulet Omnipod, Medtronic, Tandem Diabetes)

### Easy-to-Find Citations
Users can access medical sources from multiple locations:
1. **Settings > About > Medical Information & Sources** - Direct link in Settings
2. **About Modal** - "View Medical Information & Sources" link
3. **Home Screen** - Recommendation help tooltip mentions where to find sources

### Medical Disclaimer
Added clear disclaimer stating the app:
- Does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment
- Is intended as a tracking tool only
- Should not replace advice from healthcare providers

### Content Updates
- Updated AboutModal text to reference "general medical guidelines"
- Updated BodyLocation.swift comments to reference citations
- Updated help tooltip to direct users to medical sources

## Screenshots
The Medical Information view includes sections for:
- Important Disclaimer (warning banner)
- Why Rotate Infusion Sites? (with citations)
- Recommended Infusion Sites (with pump manufacturer links)
- Site Rest Periods (with citations)
- About Lipohypertrophy (with citations)
- Consult Your Healthcare Team

## Testing
- [x] Build succeeds
- [x] MedicalInformationView accessible from Settings
- [x] MedicalInformationView accessible from About Modal
- [x] All citation links are tappable and open in browser

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.13.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.13.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: in some situations, third-party code was measured when it shouldn't have
  been, slowing down test execution. This happened with layered virtual
  environments such as uv sometimes makes. The problem is fixed, closing `issue
  2082`_. Now any directory on sys.path that is inside a virtualenv is
  considered third-party code.

.. _issue 2082: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2082


.. _changes_7-13-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: when Python is installed via symlinks, for example with Homebrew, the
  standard library files could be incorrectly included in coverage reports.
  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2115`_.

- Fix: if a data file is created with no read permissions, the combine step
  would fail completely. Now a warning is issued and the file is skipped.
  Closes `issue 2117`_.

.. _issue 2115: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2115
.. _issue 2117: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2117


.. _changes_7-13-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added: the JSON report now includes a ``"start_line"`` key for function and
  class regions, indicating the first line of the region in the source. Closes
  `issue 2110`_.

- Added: The ``debug data`` command now takes file names as arguments on the
  command line, so you can inspect specific data files without needing to set
  the ``COVERAGE_FILE`` environment variable.

- Fix: the JSON report used to report module docstrings as executed lines,
  which no other report did, as described in `issue 2105`_. This is now fixed,
  thanks to Jianrong Zhao.

- Fix: coverage.py uses a more disciplined approach to detecting where
  third-party code is installed, and avoids measuring it. This shouldn't change
  any behavior. If you find that it does, please get in touch.

- Performance: data files that will be combined now record their hash as part
  of the file name. This lets us skip duplicate data more quickly, speeding the
  combining step.

- Docs: added a section explaining more about what is considered a missing
  branch and how it is reported: :ref:`branch_explain`, as requested in `issue
  1597`_. Thanks to `Ayisha Mohammed <pull 2092_>`_.

- Tests: the test suite misunderstood what core was being tested if
  ``COVERAGE_CORE`` wasn't set on 3.14+. This is now fixed, closing `issue
  2109`_.

.. _issue 1597: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1597
.. _pull 2092: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2092
.. _issue 2105: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2105
.. _issue 2109: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2109
.. _issue 2110: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2110

.. _changes_7-13-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: coverage.py now supports :file:`.coveragerc.toml` configuration
  files. These files use TOML syntax and take priority over
  :file:`pyproject.toml` but lower priority than :file:`.coveragerc` files.
  Closes `issue 1643`_ thanks to `Olena Yefymenko <pull 1952_>`_.

- Fix: we now include a permanent .pth file which is installed with the code,
  fixing `issue 2084`_.  In 7.12.1b1 this was done incorrectly: it didn't work
  when using the source wheel (``py3-none-any``).  This is now fixed. Thanks,
  `Henry Schreiner <pull 2100_>`_.

- Deprecated: when coverage.py is installed, it creates three command entry
  points: ``coverage``, ``coverage3``, and ``coverage-3.10`` (if installed for
  Python 3.10). The second and third of these are not needed and will
  eventually be removed. They still work for now, but print a message about
  their deprecation.

.. _issue 1643: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1643
.. _pull 1952: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1952
.. _pull 2100: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2100


.. _changes_7-12-1b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.1b1
   ```
   -----------------------------

- Fix: coverage.py now includes a permanent .pth file in the distribution which
  is installed with the code. This fixes `issue 2084`_: failure to patch for
  subprocess measurement when site-packages is not writable.

.. _issue 2084: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2084


.. _changes_7-12-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083
.. _pull 2085: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085
.. _issue 2086: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086
.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090
.. _issue 2091: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091


.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to

  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078

.. _changes_7-11-2:

   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

author: weter11
body:
This submission provides a reimplementation of the Rare Epic Games Launcher alternative in Rust, using the `egui` toolkit and the `legendary` CLI as a backend.

Key features:
- **Rust Backend Wrapper**: Interacts with the `legendary` CLI via `std::process::Command`, parsing JSON output for games and installation status.
- **GUI with egui**: A modern, lightweight interface featuring a searchable library, navigation sidebar, and basic settings.
- **Asynchronous Execution**: Backend calls are performed in background threads using channels to keep the UI responsive.
- **Mock Mode**: Supports a mock state for demonstration and testing when `legendary` or valid credentials are not available.
- **Login Flow**: Detects missing credentials and provides instructions to the user on how to authenticate via the CLI.

The implementation is located in the `rare-rs/` directory.

author: copilot
body:
Implement edit functionality by extending the existing new-dog screen to handle both create and edit modes via route params.

## Changes

- **Routing**: Accept `mode` ("create"|"edit") and `id` params. Defaults to create for backward compatibility.

- **Data loading**: On edit mode mount, fetch via `getDogById(id)` and prefill form. Show loading state to prevent flicker. Handle missing dog with dedicated error state.

- **Save logic**: 
  - Create: Generate new ID and timestamps
  - Edit: Preserve `id`, `metAt`, `createdAt`. Let `updateDog()` set `updatedAt`
  - Navigate to dog profile on success in both modes

- **UX**: 
  - Button text: "Save Dog" → "Save Changes" in edit mode
  - Unsaved changes prompt on cancel if form dirty
  - Disable save/cancel during async operations

- **Logging**: Added edit-specific events (`EditDog:load:*`, `EditDog:save:*`, `EditDog:camera:*`) while preserving existing create mode events.

```tsx
// Dog Profile navigates to edit mode
router.push({
  pathname: '/new-dog',
  params: { mode: 'edit', id: dog.id }
});

// Form detects mode and loads data
const mode = (params.mode as string) || 'create';
const isEditMode = mode === 'edit';

if (isEditMode && dogId) {
  const foundDog = await getDogById(dogId);
  // Prefill all fields...
}
```

**Files changed**: `app/new-dog.tsx` (+308 lines, -65 lines)

**No new dependencies**. Uses existing `getDogById()`, `updateDog()`, logging utils.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

We are building the “Dogs I’ve Met” Expo app. New Dog (create), Dogs List, and Dog Profile (view + delete) are implemented and merged.

NEXT TASK: Implement “Edit Dog” by reusing the existing New Dog screen as a shared form screen that supports both Create and Edit modes.

IMPORTANT GUIDELINES:
- Follow existing navigation approach (Expo Router or React Navigation). Do not add new navigation libraries.
- Do NOT add heavy dependencies or global state libraries.
- Keep changes minimal and localized.
- Preserve responsive behavior for portrait phones and square aspect ratio screens:
  - avoid fixed heights
  - keep form in ScrollView
  - image preview uses aspectRatio
- Use existing Dog type + storage module (/src/storage/dogs.ts):
  - getDogById(id)
  - updateDog(dog)
- Use existing logger (/src/utils/logger.ts): logEvent, logError

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 — Decide routing and params
--------------------------------------------------
We need a consistent way to open the form in edit mode.

Implement one of these patterns (choose whichever matches existing routing best):

A) A single route for the form (preferred):
   - NewDog screen accepts params:
     - mode = "create" | "edit"
     - id (required if edit)
   - Home "New Dog" uses mode="create"
   - Dog Profile "Edit" uses mode="edit" + id

OR

B) A dedicated EditDog route:
   - /edit-dog?id=<id>
   - It renders the same form component internally.

Pick the approach that best matches the current codebase with minimal change.

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 — Load existing dog in edit mode
--------------------------------------------------
When mode === "edit":
- Read id param
- On screen focus or mount:
  - logEvent("EditDog:load:start", { id })
  - call getDogById(id)
  - If not found:
    - show “Dog not found” state + button back to list
    - logEvent("EditDog:load:not_found", { id })
  - If found:
    - prefill form state:
      - name
      - breed
      - photoUri
      - metLocationText
      - notes
    - logEvent("EditDog:load:success", { id })

Ensure the form does not flicker:
- Use loading state and render form only once data is loaded.

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 — Save behavior for Edit mode
--------------------------------------------------
In edit mode, the Save button should read “Save Changes” (or still “Save Dog” if you want consistency; choose one).

On save:
- Validate required fields (name + breed).
- Construct an updated Dog object:
  - Preserve:
    - id (same)
    - metAt (do NOT change; it’s the “met timestamp”)
    - createdAt (do NOT change)
  - Update:
    - name, breed, photoUri, metLocationText, notes
    - updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()

- Call updateDog(updatedDog)

After success:
- Navigate back to Dog Profile for that id
- logEvent("EditDog:save:success", { id })

On failure:
- logError("EditDog:save:error", err, { id })
- Show alert and keep user on the form.

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 4 — Photo behavior in edit mode
--------------------------------------------------
Camera button should still work:
- Replacing the photo updates the preview and saved photoUri.
- If user cancels camera, keep existing photo.
- Do not log full URI; log length or last 12 chars.

Logging events:
- "EditDog:camera:press"
- "EditDog:camera:success"
- "EditDog:camera:cancel"
- logError("EditDog:camera:error", err)

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 5 — UX: saving indicator + disabled actions
--------------------------------------------------
Re-use the “Saving…” behavior already implemented:
- isSaving state
- disable Save and Cancel while saving
- label changes to “Saving…”

Cancel behavior:
- In create mode: go back to Home (or previous screen as current behavior)
- In edit mode: go back to Dog Profile (or previous screen)

Unsaved changes prompt (lightweight):
- If user has modified any field and presses back/cancel:
  - prompt “Discard changes?” with Discard/Keep Editing
- Keep this simple (compare initial loaded values to current state).

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 6 — Logging instrumentation
--------------------------------------------------
Add logs:
- Screen lifecycle:
  - "EditDog:screen:mount"
  - "EditDog:screen:unmount"

- Save flow:
  - "EditDog:save:press"
  - "EditDog:save:validation_failed"
  - "EditDog:save:write_start"
  - "EditDog:save:success"

- Navigation:
  - "Nav:to:DogProfile" when returning after save/cancel
  - (and any other navigation you deem important)

--------------------------------------------------
STEP 7 — Definition of Done
--------------------------------------------------
- From Dog Profile, tapping Edit opens the form with all fields prefilled.
- Editing values and saving persists changes in storage (updateDog).
- Returning to Dog Profile shows updated values.
- metAt and createdAt remain unchanged after edit.
- Works on portr...

</details>

Implementada a captura da entrada do usuário via console.

Adicionada a lógica para armazenar a string da placa na lista privada `veiculos`.

Cálculo de Tarifa: Implementada a lógica financeira utilizando a fórmula valorTotal = precoInicial + (precoPorHora * horas).

**Gerenciamento de Estado**: Adicionada a remoção efetiva do item da lista após a conclusão do pagamento.

Implementada estrutura de repetição `foreach` para percorrer e exibir todos os veículos atualmente estacionados.

Mantida a verificação prévia de lista vazia para exibir a mensagem informativa adequada.

body:
## **Description** Fixes navigation and token buyability issues in the unified buy V2 flow. **Problem 1 — Navigation error from asset details page:** When clicking the Buy button on the asset details page with unified buy V2 enabled, a navigation error occurred because `createBuildQuoteNavDetails` tried to navigate directly to the deeply nested `RampAmountInput` screen. React Navigation requires navigating through the parent route structure. **Problem 2 — Navigation from TokenSelection to input screen:** When selecting a token from the TokenSelection screen, navigation to AMOUNT_INPUT failed because it used `goToBuy` (which targets the outer route) instead of navigating directly within the same stack. **Problem 3 — Buy button shown for unsupported tokens / errors on tap:** The buyability check (`useTokenBuyability`) only used the legacy V1 token cache. When V2 was enabled, `setSelectedToken` on the RampsController would throw "Token not found" errors due to: - The ramps API returns assetIds in **lowercase**, but `parseRampIntent` produces **checksummed** addresses - Native tokens: API uses `slip44:{coinType}` but `parseRampIntent` uses `slip44:.` placeholder - The controller's `setSelectedToken` uses exact match (`===`) **Solution:** 1. Updated `createBuildQuoteNavDetails` to navigate through the proper nested route structure 2. `TokenSelection` navigates directly to `AMOUNT_INPUT` within the same stack for V2, calling `setSelectedToken` before navigating 3. `useTokenBuyability` moved to `Ramp/hooks/` (ramps domain) and updated with a unified `findMatchingRampToken` function that handles both native (chainId + slip44 namespace) and ERC20 (case-insensitive assetId) matching for V1 and V2 4. `useRampNavigation.goToBuy` resolves assetId to the controller's canonical format before calling `setSelectedToken` 5. Legacy `AssetOverview` now uses the shared `useTokenBuyability` hook instead of inline logic **Not changed:** The smart Buy button in `TokenDetails` sticky bar (`handleBuyPress`) is untouched — it routes to swaps or ramps based on user context and should not be gated by ramp buyability. ## **Changelog** CHANGELOG entry: Fixed navigation error and token buyability checks when purchasing crypto with cash using unified buy V2 ## **Related issues** Fixes: https://consensyssoftware.atlassian.net/browse/TRAM-3253 ## **Manual testing steps** ```gherkin Feature: Unified Buy V2 Navigation and Buyability Scenario: User navigates to buy flow from asset details page Given user is on asset details page with unified buy V2 feature flag enabled When user taps the cash "Buy" button on a supported token Then user should navigate to RampAmountInput screen without errors And the selected asset should be pre-filled Scenario: User selects token from token selection screen Given user is on token selection screen in unified buy V2 flow When user selects a token from the list Then user should navigate to RampAmountInput screen And the selected token should be displayed Scenario: Cash buy button hidden for unsupported tokens Given user is on asset details page for a token not supported by ramps Then the cash Buy button should not be displayed But the smart Buy/Sell sticky bar buttons should still be visible Scenario: Smart Buy button is unaffected Given user is on token details page (V2 buttons enabled) Then the sticky bar Buy button should always be visible And it should route to swaps if user has source tokens And it should route to ramps if user has no source tokens ``` ## **Screenshots/Recordings**

Unified Buy Phase 2 Navigation Bug Fix - Watch Video

### Motivation
- Prevent Tpay notification endpoint from emitting warnings or returning `FALSE` which caused failed webhook handling and inconsistent HTTP responses. 
- Ensure Tpay transaction/events are visible in the admin booking payment tab when Stripe/PayPal arrays are empty so admins can inspect Tpay activity. 
- Keep behavior minimal and consistent with existing logging and escaping practices.

### Description
- In `class/CHBS.PaymentTpay.class.php` suppressed error output (`display_errors/html_errors` + `error_reporting(0)`), set `Content-Type: text/plain`, and introduced a `$libraryAvailable` fallback instead of an immediate hard-fail.

- Changed the missing-notification-secret path to respond `200` with `TRUE` (no `FALSE` or 400), and ensured every notification exit path outputs exactly `echo 'TRUE'; exit;` (no extra whitespace or HTML).

- In `template/admin/meta_box_booking.php` added a fallback block that renders `payment_tpay_data` as a transactions table when Stripe/PayPal blocks did not render, using the same columns and detail-toggle behavior as other payment providers and escaping outputs properly.

author: flossypurse
body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive production deployment guide at `/operate/production.mdx` - **~650 lines** of practical guidance for running Resonate in production.

**Key focus:** What works today (worker scaling, PostgreSQL HA, monitoring) rather than unimplemented features (multi-server HA).

---

## What's Covered

### 1. Architecture Overview
- Server = coordination, Workers = execution
- Key insight: Workers scale horizontally, server coordinates (not a bottleneck)

### 2. Worker Scaling (PRIMARY SECTION)
**This is the critical production pattern:**
- How worker groups work
- When to scale workers (CPU, queue buildup, response times)
- Fault tolerance (crashed workers auto-reassign tasks)
- Deployment patterns:
  - Multiple processes (simple)
  - Docker containers with replicas
  - Kubernetes with HPA (5-50 workers)
  - Serverless (Cloud Run, Lambda)

### 3. Server Reliability
- PostgreSQL persistence (required for production)
- PostgreSQL HA strategies (managed services, replication)
- Backup procedures
- Health checks and metrics
- Graceful restart procedures
- When to upgrade server resources (rarely needed)

### 4. Deployment Patterns
**Complete manifests included:**
- Docker Compose (dev/staging) - full stack with healthchecks
- Kubernetes server deployment (single replica, persistent storage)
- Kubernetes worker deployment (horizontal scaling + HPA)
- Cloud Run serverless workers

### 5. Monitoring & Observability
- Prometheus metrics endpoint
- Key metrics to track (promise rate, latency, worker failures)
- Prometheus scrape config
- Logging levels and what to log
- Alert rules (server down, worker failures, DB connections)

### 6. Security in Production
- Quick checklist (auth, TLS, PostgreSQL SSL, secrets)
- Links to full security guide

### 7. What's NOT Covered (Honesty)
**Critical section** explaining unimplemented features:
- ❌ Multi-server coordination (not implemented)
- ❌ Server horizontal scaling (not needed - workers scale)
- ❌ Cross-region DR (use standard PostgreSQL patterns)
- **Why:** Worker scaling handles nearly all scale needs

---

## Key Messages

**"Focus on scaling workers"**
> In nearly all production scenarios, scaling workers horizontally is the right approach. The server coordinates work but doesn't execute it, so it rarely becomes a bottleneck.

**Realistic architecture pattern:**
- 1 Resonate server (2-4 CPU, 4-8GB RAM)
- 1 PostgreSQL database (managed service or HA replica)
- N workers (5-50+ common, scale based on load)

**Honest about limitations:**
Explicitly calls out that multi-server HA isn't implemented (rather than implying it exists or is coming soon).

---

## Code Examples Included

✅ Worker registration (TypeScript + Python)
✅ Worker group targeting
✅ Docker Compose full stack
✅ Kubernetes server deployment with healthchecks
✅ Kubernetes worker deployment with HPA
✅ Cloud Run deployment commands
✅ PostgreSQL backup scripts
✅ Prometheus scrape config
✅ Alert rules (YAML)
✅ Production security config

All examples are **copy-paste ready** and follow best practices.

---

## Addresses Audit Gap

From the docs audit, this was flagged as **high priority:**
> "Production deployment guide - MISSING (HA, scaling, DR guidance needed)"

This guide fills that gap while being **realistic** about current product capabilities:
- ✅ Scaling: Worker horizontal scaling (works great)
- ✅ HA: PostgreSQL HA/replication (standard practices)
- ✅ DR: Backup/restore procedures
- ❌ Multi-server HA: Not implemented (and likely not needed)

---

## Testing

- [x] Build passes locally
- [x] All internal links verified
- [x] Code examples follow Resonate docs style
- [x] Sentence case headings
- [x] Only `:::tip` admonitions used
- [x] All code blocks have titles

---

## Next Steps After Merge

1. Link from `/operate/run-server.mdx` to this guide
2. Link from `/operate/security.mdx` to this guide
3. Consider adding "Production Checklist" page with bullet list

---

**Estimated read time:** 15-20 minutes  
**Target audience:** Ops teams deploying Resonate in production  
**Tone:** Practical, honest, example-heavy

## Summary

Adds a `CallBuilder` abstraction for cross-platform calling convention handling and fixes Windows x64 ABI compliance issues in the dev backend.

### Key Changes

- **CallBuilder abstraction** (`src/backend/dev/CallBuilder.zig`): New module that handles platform-specific calling conventions (Windows x64 Fastcall vs System V), including:
  - Automatic shadow space allocation (Windows)
  - Return-by-pointer for large returns
  - Pass-by-pointer for large structs (Windows)
  - Correct argument register ordering per platform
  - R12 save/restore for Windows x64

- **Windows x64 ABI fixes**:
  - Fixed calling convention for 5+ argument functions
  - Fixed i128/Dec parameter passing and returns

- **sljmp module** (`src/sljmp/`): Cross-platform setjmp/longjmp for crash protection
  - Uses C library on Unix (glibc/musl)
  - Custom naked function implementation on Windows

- **aarch64 fixes**: Fixed compilation and runtime errors in aarch64 codegen

- **musl compatibility**: Use `setjmp`/`longjmp` instead of `_setjmp`/`_longjmp` for musl builds

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

`match_unmatched_activities` Lambda returns `"success": 10` indicating activities were matched, but database shows no `last_matched` updates. Users see false positives.

## Root Cause

Function uses async Lambda invocations (`InvocationType='Event'`) which return 202 when successfully queued, not when matching completes. The function counted 202 responses as successful matches.

## Changes

**Response structure updated to reflect actual behavior:**

Before:
```json
{
  "message": "Triggered matching for 10 activities",
  "success": 10,
  "failed": 0
}
```

After:
```json
{
  "message": "Queued matching for 10 activities (async - check database for actual results)",
  "queued": 10,
  "failed_to_queue": 0
}
```

- Renamed response fields: `success` → `queued`, `failed` → `failed_to_queue`
- Updated message to clarify async invocation semantics
- Enhanced function docstrings and README with async behavior documentation
- Added test suite covering queueing scenarios

## Breaking Change

Response schema changed. Any consumers expecting `success`/`failed` fields will need updates.

author: vnodesv
body:
### Motivation
- Builds can pick up a different Go runtime than the module expects, which causes stdlib compilation conflicts (e.g. `internal/abi` duplicate symbol errors) when the local `GOVERSION` differs from the module's `toolchain` pin. 
- The Makefile previously called the `go` command directly, so `make` targets could ignore the module's `toolchain` pin and trigger those mismatches.

### Description
- Add a `GOTOOLCHAIN` variable defaulting to `go1.22.0` and a `GO_CMD` wrapper (`GOTOOLCHAIN=$(GOTOOLCHAIN) go`) so `make` runs use the pinned toolchain. 
- Replace direct `go` invocations with `$(GO_CMD)` for `list`, `build`, `install`, `mod download`, `mod verify`, `install` (tools), and test targets. 
- Export `GOTOOLCHAIN` from the Makefile so subprocesses inherit the toolchain pin. 
- Keep existing build flags and target behavior unchanged aside from routing `go` through `$(GO_CMD)`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

body: The UMA.rocks voting committee members, added as reviewers to this PR, need to choose the answers for the current voting round. # Guidelines for the voting committee **TL;DR:** Make the relevant changes to this PR, then wait for the majority of reviewers to approve it, then merge it. Use comments to solve conflicts and find consensus with your fellow reviewers. **Merge needs to occur imperatively before 11:00AM UTC.** ## Select answers Go to the `Files changed` tab and click on `...` on the top-right of the json file then click on `Edit file`: The file editor opens. By default all disputes have a `P0` answer, replace it with the answer you think is the correct one: ``` { "ancillaryData": "", "question": "Will Donald Trump sign an executive order on July 11?", "answer": "" } ``` You only need to change the `answer` parameter for all elements of the array. Please do not modify the `ancillaryData` and `question` parameters. Then click `Commit changes...` at the top. A popup appears, click `Commit changes` again to confirm. Please [approve](#approve-the-answers) your own commit so that the next reviewer can directly approve and merge the pull request right away, speeding up the review process and avoiding unnecessary back-and-forth reviews. ## Solve disagreements with comments If you disagree with an answer, you can add a comment on the corresponding line by clicking the `+` icon at the beginning of the line, then write your comment and click `Add a single comment`. Use this to start a conversation with your fellow reviewers and reach a consensus for this dispute. ## Approve the answers When you agree with all the answers, go in the `Files changed` tab, click `Review changes`, write an optional comment, select the `Approve` option, and click `Submit review`. ## Merge the pull request When the majority of reviewers have approved the pull request, it is ready to be merged. Don't waste time and merge the pull request as soon as the `Merge pull request` button is enabled at the bottom of the `Conversation` tab. **Merge needs to occur imperatively before 11:00AM UTC**, otherwise the voting bot won't have any answer to commit for the pool, which means we will need to manually force push some answers & relaunch the bot manually. Ideally, this scenario should never happen. 🙂

author: natemort
body:
<!-- Describe what has changed in this PR -->
**What changed?**
- Remove DecisionsHelper. The mechanism it used for generating IDs is inconsistent with the other clients, where they all share an incrementing integer. The other functionality it provided was unused.
- Add NonDeterminism Tracking to provide specific errors when nondeterminism occurs.
  - We look at the outcome decisions for the batch and create a set of expectations that must be met so that we can immediately flag non-determinism, rather than waiting until after the user code finishing execution.
  - We add markers any time there's immediate cancellation.
- Add a state machine for Workflow completion. We need to route the Decision attributes through the DecisionManager so that it can check for nondeterminism.
- Restructure workflow exception handling a bit to handle ExceptionGroup. This still needs more work.

<!-- Tell your future self why have you made these changes -->
**Why?**
- Feature parity with other clients
- Trying out new non-determinism detection algorithm to see if it would work for other clients.

body:
Add rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@b7e9a28eded4986ec6b1fa40eeee8f8f165559ec (tag v1.0.3) to the ASF GitHub Actions allowlist.

Why: Apache Fory uses the crates.io trusted publishing flow for Rust releases and needs this action for OIDC token exchange.

Alternatives considered: Using a long-lived CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret, but the project has enabled Trusted Publishing.

Security considerations: Action is maintained by rust-lang and is pinned to an exact commit SHA per policy.

body:
## Cache Date Picker Selector Syntax

### Problem
Currently, the date picker iterates through multiple selectors every time:
- Opening date picker: tries DATE_INPUT_SELECTORS list
- Month navigation: tries PREV_MONTH_SELECTORS / NEXT_MONTH_SELECTORS lists  
- Date cells: tries DATE_CELL_SELECTORS list

This is inefficient as the same selectors are recalculated each time.

### Solution Plan
- [x] Understand existing navigation cache (already implemented in PR #2)
- [x] Add selector cache for date input buttons
- [x] Add selector cache for month navigation buttons (prev/next)
- [x] Add selector cache for date cell selectors
- [x] Update methods to check selector cache first before iterating
- [x] Create/update tests to validate selector caching
- [x] Add method to clear selector cache
- [x] Run tests to verify functionality
- [ ] Code review and security check

### Changes Made
1. Added `_selector_cache` dictionary to DatePicker `__init__` with keys:
   - `date_input`: Cache for date picker trigger button selector
   - `prev_month`: Cache for previous month button selector
   - `next_month`: Cache for next month button selector
   - `date_cell`: Cache for date cell selector

2. Updated `_open_date_picker()` to:
   - Try cached selector first
   - Cache successful selector for future use
   - Clear cache if selector becomes invalid

3. Updated `_click_month_nav()` to:
   - Try cached selector first (prev/next based on direction)
   - Cache successful selector for future use
   - Clear cache if selector becomes invalid

4. Updated `_try_pick_date_in_view()` to:
   - Try cached date cell selector first
   - Cache first successful selector
   - Clear cache if selector becomes invalid

5. Added `clear_selector_cache()` method to manually clear cached selectors:
   - Can clear specific selector type or all selectors
   - Useful when switching between different platforms or debugging

6. Added comprehensive test file `test_selector_cache.py` to verify:
   - Initial cache state
   - Cache setting and clearing
   - Cache independence across instances
   - Cache structure validation
   - Coexistence with navigation cache
   - clear_selector_cache method functionality

body:
### Motivation
- Bring the improved track animation/physics logic into `isocoaster2.jsx` so the coaster motion, telemetry and ride camera are smoother and consistent with the updated track generator and animation loop.

### Description
- Increase the friction tuning by updating `FRICTION_COEFF` from `0.0010` to `0.002` to better match the new motion characteristics. 
- Make binormal handling more robust by consolidating the `worldBinormal` check and copying+normalizing it into the transported frame to reduce frame popping in sharp curvature. 
- For non-circuit runs, reset behavior now restarts the ride at the station by setting `phys.t = 0`, restoring `phys.velocity = INITIAL_SPEED`, and clearing `phys.lastVel` so runs restart cleanly instead of dead-stopping near `t = 1`. 
- Initialize the simulation velocity vector on reset from the curve tangent (`lastVel = tangent * INITIAL_SPEED`) so the first telemetry and interpolation frames reflect a consistent starting velocity and direction.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds `WalReader` and `WalFile` to allow users to list and read WAL files. It can be used to implement change data capture. See #634 for the RFC.

Note that `mem_table_flush.rs` has been changed to flush all outstanding WAL data before a memtable is flushed. This guarantees that any data in any L0 SST will always be in the WAL first. This seems like a good property to have, and also makes it so the race condition discussed in #634 can't happen (data hits L0 but not WAL, then a failure occurs and data never makes it to WAL).

## Changes

- Add `wal_reader.rs` with `WalFile` and `WalReader`
- Update `mem_table_flush.rs` to flush all WAL files before memtables are flushed to L0

body:
## Summary

- Replace Alpine container builds with cargo-zigbuild for Linux musl static linking
- Use Zig's bundled musl libc instead of building inside Alpine containers
- Enables standard cargo caching (no more fresh Rust installs per build)
- Maintains workflow uniformity with macOS/Windows builds

## Changes

- **Add** `.github/actions/setup-zig/action.yml` - new action for Zig installation (pinned to 0.14.0)
- **Update** `.github/workflows/reflow-rust.yml` - use cargo-zigbuild for Linux builds
- **Update** `.github/scripts/verify-static-linking.sh` - work on Ubuntu with musl target directories
- **Update** `.cargo/config.toml` - clarify comments about Zig redundancy
- **Update** `docs/src/project/ci.md` - document new tooling
- **Remove** `.github/scripts/alpine-build.sh` - no longer needed
- **Remove** `.github/actions/setup-rust/setup.sh` - only used for Alpine builds

## Rationale

| Aspect | Before (Alpine) | After (cargo-zigbuild) |
|--------|-----------------|------------------------|
| Build environment | Docker container | Native Ubuntu runner |
| Rust installation | Fresh install each build | Runner toolchain (cached) |
| Linker | Alpine's musl-gcc | Zig's bundled musl |
| Caching | None | Standard cargo caching |
| musl version control | Alpine release | Zig version pin |

## Testing

The CI will validate this change by running on the PR:
- Linux build jobs complete with cargo-zigbuild
- Static linking verification passes
- Tests pass in both glibc and musl environments
- No regressions on macOS/Windows

## Notes

- Alpine container **tests** are kept - testing musl binaries in a musl environment is still valuable
- Zig version 0.14.0 is pinned for reproducibility

Closes #57

body:
## 🚀 新增功能：AI助手消息类型支持

### 解决的问题
随着AI助手（如Clawdbot、ChatGPT等）在GitHub workflows中的普及，现有的消息类型无法很好地展示AI生成的复杂内容，如代码块、结构化数据、任务状态等。

### 新增功能
1. **新的msg_type**: `ai_assistant`
2. **结构化消息格式**: 支持header、summary、code、metrics、text、divider、actions等多种章节
3. **代码高亮**: 自动识别编程语言并高亮显示
4. **任务状态跟踪**: 显示pending/running/completed/failed状态
5. **交互式按钮**: 支持快速操作按钮

### 使用示例
```yaml
- name: AI Assistant Message
  uses: Open-Source-Bazaar/feishu-action@feature/ai-assistant-message
  with:
    url: ${{ secrets.FEISHU_BOT_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    msg_type: ai_assistant
    content: |
      ai_assistant:
        title: "代码审查报告"
        assistant: "Clawdbot"
        status: "completed"
        sections:
          - type: "header"
            text: "审查完成"
          
          - type: "code"
            language: "typescript"
            code: |
              const result = calculate();
            suggestions:
              - "使用const声明不变的值"
          
          - type: "metrics"
            items:
              - label: "代码质量"
                value: "85/100"
                trend: "+5"
```

### 技术实现
- 新增 `src/ai-assistant.ts` - AI助手消息转换器
- 扩展 `src/main.ts` - 支持新的消息类型
- 更新 `action.yml` - 添加ai_assistant到支持的msg_type
- 添加 `__tests__/ai-assistant.test.ts` - 完整的单元测试
- 更新 `README.md` - 详细的使用文档

M  README.md

Documents the technical and business requirements for integrating live market data into SellAmericaApp, covering data sources, costs, and implementation strategy.

## Changes

- **New file**: `SellAmericaApp-LiveData-Requirements.md`
  - API sources: FRED (free), TIC (free), Bloomberg/Reuters ($24K/year), CFTC (free), Gold APIs ($10-30/mo), sentiment analysis ($99+/mo)
  - Cost-effective alternatives: Alpha Vantage, Quandl, Yahoo Finance as proxies for premium data
  - Implementation phases: Mock data setup, API wrapper development, caching strategy, UI integration
  - Budget breakdown and 5-week timeline

## Key Technical Details

The plan prioritizes free government sources (FRED, TIC, CFTC) for core economic indicators while identifying low-cost alternatives to expensive professional terminals. Includes FastAPI caching strategy with tiered refresh intervals based on data frequency.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

The text below discusses the live data needs of the SellAmericaApp. Create a file to include this information as part of the repository as a .md file. 




Here is a detailed plan to make this part of the application work with live data using the specified sources, including identifying data brokers and potential costs:

---

### **Step 1: Assess Available APIs and Data Integrations**
1. **Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)**  
   - **API**: Investigate the FRED API provided by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.  
     - Authentication: Requires free API key registration.
     - Endpoints of interest: Currency signals, interest rate data, and economic indicators.
     - **Costs**: Free.
     - **Next Step**: Read the developer documentation to identify required endpoints (e.g., DXY proxies, yield curve dynamics).

2. **Treasury International Capital (TIC) System**  
   - **Access**: TIC data is entirely free and published monthly.
   - **Format**: Review available information and formats (CSV/Excel) on the U.S. Treasury website.
   - **Challenges**: Slight data lag as TIC is updated on a delayed basis (~1 month).
   - **Next Step**: Analyze historical data for integration and set up workflows for monthly updates.

3. **Bloomberg/Reuters Market Data**  
   - **Access**: Both platforms provide comprehensive market data including DXY movements, Treasury yields, ETF flows, and more.
   - **Costs**: Requires professional subscription.
     - Bloomberg Terminal: ~$24,000/year.
     - Reuters Eikon: Similar pricing.
     - **Next Step**: Evaluate if costs are justified or look for lower-cost proxies from platforms like Alpha Vantage, Quandl, or Yahoo Finance APIs (some free, others with tiered pricing).

4. **CFTC Commitments of Traders Reports**  
   - **Access**: Free, available online.
   - **Challenges**: Provided weekly in CSV format with no direct API.
   - **Next Step**: Automate parsing and processing of CSV files into the system.

5. **World Gold Council Data**  
   - **Access**: Check the availability of live gold prices and historical trends.
   - **Costs**: World Gold Council may require membership or purchase for comprehensive data. Other alternatives include free APIs like GoldAPI or paid platforms such as Xignite for better reliability.
   - **Next Step**: Compare free versus premium gold price sources based on requirements.

6. **News APIs for Sentiment Analysis**  
   - **Access**: Use sentiment analysis APIs from providers like:
     - Google News API or ContextualWebNews API (free/low-cost tiers for searching headlines).
     - Advanced sentiment solutions like Aylien, AWS Comprehend, or Microsoft Azure (paid).
   - **Costs**: 
     - Aylien: ~$99/month for baseline features.
     - Azure/AWS: Pay-per-request (~$1 to $3 per 1,000 API calls).
   - **Next Step**: Trial multiple APIs for sentiment accuracy and integration flexibility.

---

### **Step 2: Mock Data Analysis and Transition Plan**
1. **Create Mock Data**  
   - Populate `/data` directory with realistic timestamps and values.
   - Include proxies and explain missing data with a "Limitations" section.

2. **Develop an API Wrapper**  
   - Centralized fetch module to interface with live APIs.  
     - Example: `fetchFREDData`, `fetchGoldPrice`.

3. **Test and Validate with Static Data**  
   - Test mock datasets for algorithm accuracy.
   - Validate scoring logic (e.g., Signal Strength: 0-100).

---

### **Step 3: Broker and Subscription Evaluation**
1. Compare Alternatives  
   - For Bloomberg/Reuters costs, consider partial substitutes like:
     - Alpha Vantage: Free/basic, $75/month for premium.
     - Quandl: Free/basic, $50-$300/month for premium datasets.
     - Yahoo Finance API: Free tier available.
   - World Gold Council's premium data can be replaced with GoldAPI (~$10/month as a start).

2. **Contact Major Brokers**  
   - Reach out to Bloomberg/Reuters teams for custom packages.
   - Establish partnerships, potentially lowering subscription tiers for smaller data pulls.

3. Use Open Data Sources for Core Needs  
   - Consolidate free avenues (FRED, TIC, CFTC).

---

### **Step 4: Build the System for Live Data**
1. Implement Caching  
   - Use FastAPI routes to cache fetched data for frequently updated APIs.
   - Setup refresh intervals based on:
     - High-frequency: Currency movements (every few minutes via free APIs).
     - Low-frequency: TIC reports (~monthly).

2. Design Limitations Messaging  
   - Provide disclaimers where proxies are used instead of actual data.

3. **UI Integrations**  
   - Update charts and dashboard components with live data layers.
   - Add “Data Freshness” and “Data Limitations” badges where required.

---

### **Step 5: Budget and Timeline**
1. **Initial Costs**  
   - Free sources (FRED/TIC/CFTC) setup: $0.
   - Additional sources:
     - GoldAPI or similar: ~$10-$30/month.
     - Sentiment analysis APIs: Trial->Premium (~$99+).

author: justadudeinspace
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a small, shared core shell library for the cockpit codepath to centralize common helpers and avoid duplication.
- Offer stable identity constants and repo-relative path resolution so scripts can locate repo resources reliably.
- Implement portable, Termux- and macOS-friendly shell utilities for command checks, time, and temporary files.
- Add standardized logging, robust platform detection, `.env` parsing with precedence, and a flight recorder for run artifacts.

### Description
- Add `cockpit/core/constants.sh` which exports stable constants and path helpers including `axiom_script_dir`, `axiom_cockpit_dir`, `axiom_repo_root`, `axiom_config_dir`, `axiom_runs_dir`, and `axiom_locker_dir`.
- Add `cockpit/core/shell.sh` with helpers `axiom_command_exists`, `axiom_is_tty_stdout`, `axiom_is_tty_stdin`, `axiom_require_command`, `axiom_safe_mkdir`, `axiom_now_utc`, and a `axiom_mktemp` compatibility wrapper.
- Add `cockpit/core/log.sh` providing `axiom_log_info`, `axiom_log_warn`, `axiom_log_error`, and `axiom_die` with a consistent `[axiom][<level>]` format.
- Add `cockpit/core/platform.sh` with detection helpers `axiom_is_termux`, `axiom_is_proot`, `axiom_is_wsl`, `axiom_is_linux`, `axiom_is_macos`, `axiom_is_windows`, plus `axiom_detect_platform` and `axiom_platform_summary`.
- Add `cockpit/core/env.sh` implementing `.env` parsing with `axiom_load_env_file`, `axiom_env_get`, `axiom_env_bool`, and `axiom_ensure_env_file`, honoring existing environment variables and handling quoted values and inline comments.
- Add `cockpit/core/runs.sh` flight-recorder utilities `axiom_runs_dir_path`, `axiom_runs_create_dir`, `axiom_runs_write_output`, `axiom_runs_write_metadata`, and `axiom_runs_log_ai`, and ensure runs directories are created when needed (this is the only module with side effects).
- Add `cockpit/core/README.md` documenting purpose, file responsibilities, the side-effect rule, recommended sourcing order, and a short usage example.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed against these new helper scripts in this change.

author: tacogips
body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 7 of the SDK development, adding programmatic tool registration capabilities that enable TypeScript applications to define and register custom MCP tools at runtime without modifying Claude Code configuration files. The implementation provides a complete bidirectional control protocol between the SDK and Claude Code CLI subprocess, allowing external applications to handle tool calls in-process with full session state management.

## Changes

This PR introduces a comprehensive SDK infrastructure for programmatic tool integration:

### Core Tool Registration System
- tool() factory function - Type-safe tool definition with input schema validation and handler registration
- createSdkMcpServer() - Creates in-process MCP server configurations from SDK tool definitions
- ToolRegistry class - Internal registry managing tool lifecycle and lookup by fully-qualified names

### Transport and Protocol Layer
- SubprocessTransport - Spawns Claude Code CLI as subprocess using Bun.spawn()
- ControlProtocolHandler - Bidirectional JSON-RPC message routing between SDK and CLI
- Request/Response lifecycle management - Async request tracking with timeout handling
- MCP message handling - Routes tools/call requests to registered handlers

### Session State Management
- SessionStateManager - State machine implementation for session lifecycle tracking
- State transitions - Manages idle to running to waiting_tool_call to completed flows
- PendingToolCall tracking - Records active tool calls awaiting results
- SessionStats - Tracks token usage, cost, message count, and tool call metrics

### High-Level Client APIs
- ClaudeCodeToolAgent - Single-session agent with MCP server registration
- ToolAgentSession - Represents an active session with state monitoring
- ClaudeCodeClient - Multi-turn interactive client with context preservation
- Event system integration - Emits tool_started, tool_completed events

### Type System
- SdkTool interface - Generic tool definition with typed input schemas
- ToolInputSchema - Supports simple type mappings and full JSON Schema
- ToolResult and ToolResultContent - Structured tool outputs
- McpServerConfig variants - Union type supporting stdio, HTTP, SSE, and SDK servers
- Control protocol types - Complete JSON-RPC 2.0 message type definitions

### Testing Infrastructure
- MockTransport - In-memory transport simulating CLI communication
- MockClaudeSession - Scenario-based session simulator for integration testing
- Test scenarios - Pre-defined conversation flows
- 449 new tests - Comprehensive unit and integration tests (2385 total passing)
- Mock fixtures - Reusable test utilities in src/sdk/__fixtures__/

### Documentation and Planning
- design-docs/spec-sdk-tools.md - Complete specification
- impl-plans/sdk-tools.md - Detailed implementation plan
- Updated PROGRESS.json - Phase 7 implementation status tracking

| src/sdk/types/tool.ts | 392 | 0 | Define SDK tool types |

## Technical Details

### Architecture Decisions

**Subprocess Transport Strategy**: Uses Bun.spawn() for Claude Code CLI subprocess management instead of Node child_process for better performance and native TypeScript support. Handles stdin/stdout JSON-RPC streams with proper backpressure and error handling.

**State Machine Design**: SessionStateManager implements explicit state transitions to enable accurate waiting for tool call detection. This allows SDK users to distinguish between normal processing and tool execution states.

**Type Safety**: All SDK types use maximum TypeScript strictness. Generic type parameters on SdkTool enable type-safe tool handlers with autocomplete support.

**Protocol Design**: Implements full JSON-RPC 2.0 bidirectional protocol with method namespacing to distinguish between MCP tool calls and SDK control messages.

**Testing Strategy**: Two-tier approach with MockTransport for unit tests and MockClaudeSession for integration tests simulating complete conversation flows.

### Key Implementation Patterns

**Factory Functions**: tool() and createSdkMcpServer() follow functional factory pattern for immutable configuration objects.

**Event-Driven Architecture**: ControlProtocolHandler uses EventEmitter for tool_call and tool_result events, allowing external monitoring and logging.

**Async Iteration**: ClaudeCodeClient provides async iterator interface for streaming Claude responses.

**Graceful Degradation**: All timeouts and error conditions are properly handled with specific error types.

### Dependencies

No new external dependencies added. Implementation uses only existing project dependencies.

## Related Issues/PRs

---

## Additional Notes

This completes Phase 7 of the SDK roadmap, establishing the foundation for programmatic tool registration. Future phases will build on this infrastructure.

The SDK now provides all necessary primitives for embedding Claude Code in external TypeScript applications, enabling use cases like custom workflow engines, testing frameworks, interactive applications, and multi-project orchestration.

All tests pass: 2385 tests, 5287 expect() calls.

body:
## Summary
Makes it easier to evaluate scraping performance and keeps the database tidy by automatically removing old scrape history.

## Problem
The scrape history page only showed 20 entries per page, making it difficult to see trends or compare multiple scrapes for the same board. Additionally, the database was accumulating every scrape log ever created with no cleanup mechanism.

When initially increasing pagination to 100, Python 3.14's stricter async/threading handling exposed inefficient queries (N+1 COUNT queries) causing runtime errors.

## Solution
- Increased pagination to 50 items (enough to see multiple scrapes per board while maintaining performance)
- Optimized queries to use annotated counts and better prefetching
- Added automatic cleanup that runs probabilistically during normal scraping (10% chance) to delete logs older than 600 days
- Changed ordering to use indexed primary key instead of unindexed `created` field

## Test plan
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Scrape history page loads without async errors
- [x] Verified query optimization eliminates N+1 queries

Closes #134

author: hahaschool
body:
## Summary
- Fix pagination not working for `list_items` API
- The Slack API returns `next_cursor` in `response_metadata`, not at the response top level
- Correctly determine `has_more` based on cursor presence

## Problem
Previously, the code looked for `next_cursor` and `has_more` at the top level of the API response:
```python
"has_more": response.get("has_more", False),
"next_cursor": response.get("next_cursor"),
```

But Slack API actually returns pagination info in `response_metadata`:
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "items": [...],
  "response_metadata": {
    "next_cursor": "bGlzdF9pZDo5MTUy..."
  }
}
```

## Solution
Extract cursor from the correct location:
```python
response_metadata = response.get("response_metadata", {})
next_cursor = response_metadata.get("next_cursor", "")
has_more = bool(next_cursor)
```

## Test plan
- [x] Tested with 700+ archived items - successfully paginated through all 7 pages
- [x] All 58 existing tests pass

## Summary

Adds comprehensive GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow with smart path filtering and Turborepo optimization.

## Features

✅ **Smart Path Filtering** - Only runs tests for changed code
✅ **Full Suite on Main** - Ensures production quality  
✅ **Turborepo Optimization** - Caches build outputs for faster runs
✅ **Playwright E2E Tests** - Automated browser testing
✅ **PostgreSQL Service** - Tests run against real database
✅ **Concurrency Control** - Cancels outdated runs automatically

## Workflow Jobs

1. **Detect Changes** - Identifies which packages changed using `dorny/paths-filter`
2. **Quality Checks** - ESLint + TypeScript (uses `--affected` on PRs)
3. **Unit Tests** - API tests (conditional on API changes)
4. **E2E Tests** - Playwright (conditional on API/web changes)
