body:
## Summary
This PR adds a "Nearby Airports" feature that displays airports within a 30 nautical mile radius of the currently selected airport, allowing users to quickly navigate to nearby alternatives.

## Key Changes
- **New server action `getNearbyAirports()`** in `src/app/actions.ts`
  - Implements Haversine formula to calculate great-circle distances between airports
  - Returns up to 10 nearby airports sorted by distance
  - Filters out airports without valid coordinates
  
- **New `NearbyAirport` interface** for type-safe nearby airport data
  - Includes ICAO code, name, city, state, and distance in nautical miles

- **New `NearbyAirports` component** in `src/components/NearbyAirports.tsx`
  - Client component that fetches and displays nearby airports
  - Shows loading state while fetching data
  - Displays first 5 airports with expandable "Show more" button
  - Each airport is clickable to navigate to that airport's data
  - Responsive design with hover effects and smooth transitions
  - Handles race conditions with fetch ID tracking

- **Integration into `WindPlot` component**
  - Renders `NearbyAirports` component below runway wind table
  - Passes current ICAO and selection handler for seamless navigation

## Implementation Details
- Distance calculations use nautical miles (Earth's radius: 3440.065 nm)
- Distances are rounded to 1 decimal place for readability
- Component gracefully handles missing coordinate data
- Uses ref-based fetch ID tracking to prevent stale state updates
- Styling matches existing dark theme with Twitter-inspired colors

author: rajasunrise
body:
This PR enhances the security of the application by mitigating a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.

**Vulnerability:**
Previously, the `StationCamera` model allowed any URL with valid schemes (`rtsp`, `http`, etc.). This could allow a malicious administrator (or an attacker who compromised an admin account) to configure a camera with a URL pointing to `localhost` or internal services. Since the server uses `ffmpeg` to connect to these URLs, this could be used to scan internal ports or access sensitive internal endpoints (like cloud metadata services at `169.254.169.254`).

**Fix:**
The `validateRTSPURL` function in `internal/models/models.go` has been updated to:
1.  Parse the hostname from the URL.
2.  Reject the hostname "localhost".
3.  Parse the IP address and reject if it is a Loopback address, Link-Local Unicast address, or Unspecified address.
4.  Standard private IPs (e.g., `192.168.x.x`) are still allowed to support local camera deployments.

**Verification:**
The `TestRTSPURLValidation` test in `internal/models/models_test.go` was updated to verify that `tcp://127.0.0.1:1234` and `rtsp://localhost:554` are now rejected.

author: jlowin
body:
When `fastmcp run --reload --port 8002` detects a file change, the old server process needs to fully release the port before the new one starts. The reload mechanism was calling `process.kill()` (SIGKILL) on just the direct child, but when the command is wrapped with `uv run`, the actual server is a grandchild — SIGKILL kills `uv`, the server becomes an orphan still holding the port, and the new process gets "address already in use."

The fix puts the subprocess in its own process group (`start_new_session=True`) and sends SIGTERM to the entire group on reload, giving all processes in the tree a chance to shut down gracefully and release ports. Falls back to SIGKILL after 3 seconds if needed.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent players from landing safely when the square clips a platform edge or just grazes the side of a cube to make gameplay more predictable and fair.

### Description
- Add an `edgeBuffer` calculation and `isOverSafeSurface` boolean to require the square be centered on a cube when counting a landing. 
- Require `isOverSafeSurface` in the cube-landing condition so partial edge landings no longer count as safe landings. 
- Tighten collision handling so side impacts or collisions while not firmly on the platform (or when the platform differs) trigger game over.
- Changes are limited to `tyler-dash.html` (landing/collision logic around obstacle handling).

### Testing
- Launched a local server with `python -m http.server 8000` and loaded the page at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/tyler-dash.html` using a Playwright script. 
- Playwright ran and produced a screenshot at `artifacts/tyler-dash-safe-landing.png`, confirming the page loads; no runtime errors observed during the load.

body: I hereby agree to the terms of the CLA available at: https://docs.databend.com/dev/policies/cla/ ## Summary This PR refactors virtual column refresh into a two‑phase workflow (prepare + commit) to reduce conflicts with concurrent writes, and switches the virtual column file prefix from `_vb` to `_vb_v2` to safely refresh legacy data. - Two‑phase refresh: - Prepare builds virtual column files and draft metas without table locks. - Commit re-reads the latest snapshot and applies metadata updates quickly under a short lock. This shortens the lock window and reduces write contention. - Conflict handling: commit now allows OCC retries for concurrent inserts instead of failing immediately. - Prefix bump: virtual column files are now stored under `_vb_v2`; legacy `_vb` files are detected and skipped during refresh to avoid stale metadata. fixes: #[Link the issue here] ## Tests - [x] Unit Test - [x] Logic Test - [ ] Benchmark Test - [ ] No Test - _Explain why_ ## Type of change - [ ] Bug Fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New Feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking Change (fix or feature that could cause existing functionality not to work as expected) - [ ] Documentation Update - [x] Refactoring - [ ] Performance Improvement - [ ] Other (please describe): - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/databendlabs/databend/19395)

# Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

## Summary
Successfully implemented Vercel Web Analytics for the Aberturas Gutiérrez static HTML website.

## Changes Made

### Modified Files:
- **index.html** - Added Vercel Web Analytics tracking scripts

## Implementation Details

Since this is a plain HTML website (no framework), I added the Vercel Web Analytics scripts directly to the `<head>` section of the index.html file, following the official Vercel documentation for HTML sites.

### Added Code:
```html
<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->
<script>
    window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

The scripts were added after the font stylesheet link and before the custom styles section in the `<head>` tag.

## Technical Notes

1. **No Package Installation Required**: For plain HTML sites, the `@vercel/analytics` package is not needed. The tracking script is loaded directly from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`.

2. **Route Support**: Note that plain HTML implementation does not include automatic route support, but this is acceptable for a single-page website.

3. **Line Endings**: The original file had Windows-style line endings (CRLF), which were converted to Unix-style (LF) for consistency.

4. **Tracking Activation**: Once deployed to Vercel with Analytics enabled in the dashboard:
   - The script will automatically load from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`
   - Page views will be tracked automatically
   - A Fetch/XHR request to `/_vercel/insights/view` should be visible in browser DevTools

## Next Steps

After deployment:
1. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard (Project → Analytics → Enable)
2. Deploy the site to Vercel
3. Verify tracking by checking browser Network tab for `/_vercel/insights/view` requests
4. View analytics data in the Vercel dashboard under the Analytics tab

## No Build Steps Required

This is a static HTML site with no package.json or build process:
- No dependencies to install
- No build commands to run
- No lock files to update
- Site is ready to deploy as-is

## Overview

- `get_issue`: Get single issue/PR
- `create_issue`: Create new issue
- `close_issue`: Close issue/PR
- `get_pull_request`: Get PR details
- `get_file`: Get file content
- `create_or_update_file`: Create/update file

## Summary
Fixes invisible output for `TableOfContents(aside=false)` and adds tests.

## Changes

### PlutoServer
- **Rich output**: `extractOutput` now handles Pluto's MIME-keyed format (e.g. `{"text/html": "<script>..."}`) so TableOfContents and similar outputs are not dropped.
- **Output subfield patches**: `handleOutputSubField` accepts MIME-type subfields (e.g. `["cell_results", id, "output", "text/html"]`).
- **Patch order**: `notebook_diff` patches are applied in two passes (output subfields first, then others) so execution does not end with 0 outputs when Pluto sends `running=false` before `output.body`/`output.mime`.

### Renderer
- **TableOfContents display**: When output is script-only (PlutoUI TableOfContents), show a placeholder or build an interactive TOC from `h1`/`h2`/`h3` in other `.pluto-output` containers in the same document. Label: "Index".
- **pluto-toc-utils**: Extracted `isTableOfContentsLike(html)` into `src/pluto-toc-utils.ts` for unit testing without DOM.

### Tests
- `pluto-toc-utils.test.ts`: 8 tests for `isTableOfContentsLike`.
- `pluto-server.test.ts`: 4 tests for `extractOutput` rich output and fallback MIME.

## Description

This PR fixes flaky async tests on Windows CI by replacing time-based sleeps (e.g. `asyncio.sleep(0.1)`) with deterministic condition-based waiting.

The failures were caused by platform-dependent async scheduling differences between Linux and Windows, which led to assertions running before async side effects (such as event handlers or batched cache flushes) had completed.

This change improves test reliability across platforms without modifying any production logic.

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)

---

## Related Issues

Fixes #3470 

---

## Changes Made

- Replaced fixed `asyncio.sleep(0.1)` calls used for synchronization in async tests with deterministic `wait_until(...)` conditions.
- Ensured async event handlers and background batch flushes complete before assertions are evaluated.
- Replaced sleep-based task yielding with `asyncio.sleep(0)` where only event loop yielding was required.
- Reformatted affected test files using `ruff format` to satisfy CI formatting checks.

---

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimization achieves a **113% speedup** by replacing NumPy's array-based cumsum/searchsorted approach with an early-exit loop that accumulates histogram bins incrementally.

**Key Change**: Instead of computing `cumsum = np.cumsum(hist)` (which allocates a full cumulative array) and then `np.searchsorted(cumsum, target_count)`, the optimized code iterates through bins, accumulating counts until reaching the target:

```python

```

**Why This is Faster**:

1. **Memory allocation reduction**: The original code always allocates a full cumsum array (size n_bins). The optimized version only uses a scalar accumulator, eliminating this allocation overhead.

2. **Early termination benefit**: For **low quantiles** (1st, 10th, 50th percentile), the loop breaks early without processing all bins. The test results confirm this - cases that break in the first few bins show **200-400% speedup**, while high quantiles (99th percentile) that scan most bins show slower performance (45% slower in `test_large_scale_precision_test_99percent_quantile`).

3. **Reduced NumPy overhead**: The original code calls two NumPy functions (cumsum + searchsorted). The optimized version uses a simple Python loop with float conversions, which for moderate-sized histograms (typical case: 5000 bins as per `num_quantile_bins` default) has lower overhead.

**Trade-offs by Quantile Position**:
- **Low quantiles (1%-50%)**: Excellent speedup (200-300% faster) due to early exit
- **High quantiles (90%-99%)**: Slower performance when scanning many bins (45-70% slower in 99th percentile cases with 200+ bins)
- **Median quantiles**: Moderate speedup (200% faster) as the loop scans roughly half the bins

**Impact on Workloads**: This optimization is most beneficial when `_compute_single_quantile` is called repeatedly for **lower quantiles** (which is common in statistical analysis where median and lower percentiles are frequently computed). The function computes quantiles from histograms maintained by `RunningQuantileStats`, so batch processing scenarios that track 1st, 10th, and 50th percentiles will see substantial gains. ### Motivation
- Provide a single source of truth for UI menu data instead of hardcoded client lists by exposing a backend endpoint that composes menu from `settings_modules`, `settings_pages` and the current user permissions. 
- Prevent the sidebar from disappearing on navigation and make it behave like a real app-level navigation (collapsed, expanded and hover-preview states).
- Ensure module links (e.g. `products`, `warehouse`) open in-app without forcing the UI to hardcode menu entries.

### Description
- Added a new backend endpoint `GET /api/core/v1/navigation` in `core/modules/settings/routes.js` that builds navigation from `settings_modules` + `settings_pages` and filters pages by permission using existing `canAccess` logic. 
- Extended UI API with `NavigationItem` type and `fetchNavigation()` in `ui/src/app/api.ts` to consume the new endpoint. 
- Reworked the sidebar to fetch navigation dynamically and render groups/children from backend data in `ui/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx`, including an icon resolver and improved label fallback/translation logic. 
- Changed shell/sidebar state handling in `ui/src/layout/Shell.tsx` to support a persistent collapsed state (prop `collapsed` / `data-collapsed`) and removed the behavior that removed the sidebar from the DOM on collapse. 
- Added `ui/src/pages/ModulePlaceholder.tsx` and routes in `ui/src/app/App.tsx` to keep module routes in-app (`/:module` and `/:module/:page`) while modules are implemented. 
- Updated styles in `ui/src/styles/theme.css` to use CSS variables for sidebar width, implement fixed positioning, width transitions, icon layout, and a hover-preview overlay that does not alter layout or remove the sidebar from the DOM.

The `services/fund.js` file was empty with a syntax error placeholder (`term = ...;` on line 17), preventing module loading. Implemented complete API service layer with 7 functions integrating TianTian Fund's public APIs.

## Implementation

**Core API Functions:**
- `getFundValuation` - Real-time valuation via JSONP endpoint
- `getBatchFundValuation` - Parallel batch fetch with 5min cache
- `searchFund` - Fund search via EastMoney API
- `getFundHistory` - Historical NAV with fallback to detail endpoint

- `getFundRank` - Rankings with 30min cache

- JSONP parsing: strips `jsonpgz()` wrapper and `jQuery()` callbacks
- JavaScript variable extraction: regex-based for fund detail page format
- Promise-wrapped `wx.request` for async/await support
- Timezone-safe date formatting via `formatDate()` helper
- Graceful degradation: returns empty arrays on API failures

```javascript
// Input: jsonpgz({"fundcode":"004814","name":"中欧红利优享混合A",...});
const jsonStr = data.replace(/^jsonpgz\(/, '').replace(/\);?$/, '');
const result = JSON.parse(jsonStr);

body:
### Motivation
- The citation popup could grow taller than the viewport and be partially unreachable on long pages. 
- Copy actions should immediately close the popup and surface a brief toast so users know the citation was copied. 
- The popup must be robust on heavy CSS sites and avoid leaking page scroll or overlays after close.

### Description
- Reworked modal CSS to use scoped `.web-unlocker-*` classes with a fixed backdrop (`.web-unlocker-backdrop { inset: 0; }`), stronger z-indexes, and `pointer-events: auto` to ensure overlay precedence. 
- Converted popup into a modal shell with header, close button, scrollable body (`.web-unlocker-popup-body { overflow-y: auto; flex: 1 1 auto; }`), `max-height: 85vh`, `width: min(720px, 92vw)`, and `overflow: hidden` on the popup so header/footer remain fixed. 
- Added a header close button and backdrop click handler that only closes when clicking the backdrop root, plus `popup.focus()` for basic focus management and ESC handling via existing `handleKeydown`. 
- Implemented `lockPageScroll()` / `unlockPageScroll()` to prevent page scrolling while the modal is open and restore state on close, and wired `lockPageScroll()` at popup open and `unlockPageScroll()` on `closePopup()`. 
- On successful copy the code now shows a format-specific toast (e.g. `Citation copied (APA).`) and closes the popup immediately; failures keep the popup open and surface an error toast. 
- Adjusted button scoping/styles so modal buttons use `.web-unlocker-popup-body button` and `.web-unlocker-footer button` to reduce interference with page CSS. 
- All changes are contained to `extension/content/unlock_content.js` and only touch the content script and its injected CSS; citation generation and backend messaging remain unchanged.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this content-script change (manual verification recommended on live pages to validate viewport sizing, copy behavior, backdrop clicks, and scroll locking).

### Motivation

- Provide a small local Web UI to inspect system status and live logs using React + Vite + TypeScript. 
- Keep API usage simple and local-friendly by using relative `/api` endpoints and a Vite dev proxy to the backend at `http://localhost:8080` so developers can run the UI without changing backend URLs.
- Ensure dependencies use permissive licenses (MIT/Apache-2.0 family) and avoid GPL dependencies.

### Description

- Scaffolds a new frontend under `frontend/` including `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.node.json`, `index.html`, and TypeScript React sources. 
- Adds routing with React Router and two pages: `/` (`StatusPage`) which fetches `GET /api/status`, and `/logs` (`LogsPage`) which subscribes to `GET /api/stream/logs` via `EventSource` (SSE). 
- Configures Vite dev server proxy to forward all `/api` requests to `http://localhost:8080` (SSE-compatible) in `vite.config.ts`. 
- Adds UI styling in `src/styles.css`, TypeScript vite env types in `src/vite-env.d.ts`, and documentation in `frontend/README.md` describing install/run steps using Yarn. 
- Adjusts `package.json` build script to run TypeScript checks before `vite build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && vite build`).

### Testing

- Attempted `yarn install` in `frontend/` to fetch dependencies, but it failed with a registry `403` error so dependencies were not installed and the dev server was not started.

body:
## Summary
Vendor checkout was failing in production with `StripeInvalidRequestError` / "No such customer" when the stored `vendors.stripe_customer_id` referred to a customer that no longer exists in the current Stripe account (e.g. wrong mode or migrated account).

This hotfix makes vendor checkout resilient:
- **Before** using the stored customer id, we call `stripe.customers.retrieve()`. If it fails with `resource_missing` or "No such customer", we treat the stored id as invalid.
- **Recovery:** create a new Stripe customer (user email + metadata), persist to `vendors.stripe_customer_id`, then create the Checkout Session with the new customer id. Only one recovery per request (no retry loop).
- **Logging:** when recovery runs, we log `[stripe/checkout] recovered_missing_customer` with `requestId`, `oldCustomerSuffix`, `newCustomerSuffix` (suffix only, no full ids).

Consumer checkout is unchanged (this route is vendor-only; consumer uses other endpoints).

## Verification

### Local / PR
- `npm ci` and `npm run build` pass.

### Quick production smoke test (after deploy)
1. Open **https://goodhempdistro.com/pricing?tab=vendor**
2. Click **"Start checkout"** for Vendor Starter monthly.
3. **Expected:** redirect to Stripe Checkout page (session URL) with no error modal.

### Post-merge (Vercel logs)
- Confirm there are no 500s for `POST /api/stripe/checkout` for vendor flows.
- If a bad customer id was present, the log `recovered_missing_customer` should appear and the second attempt (session create with new customer) succeeds.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches Stripe checkout flow and persistence of `vendors.stripe_customer_id`; a bad error classification or customer creation/update failure could impact subscription creation for vendors, but changes are localized and add defensive handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Vendor Stripe Checkout is now resilient to stale/missing stored customer IDs.** The API route validates `vendors.stripe_customer_id` via `stripe.customers.retrieve()` and, on "missing customer"-style errors, clears it and creates a fresh Stripe customer before creating the Checkout Session.
> 
> Adds targeted detection (`isStripeMissingCustomerError`), includes `plan_type: "vendor"` metadata on created customers, and logs a recovery warning (`recovered_missing_customer`) with only customer ID suffixes for safer debugging.
>

# Simplify Config Loader to JSON-Only Format

## Summary

This PR removes JavaScript config file support and simplifies the config loader to JSON-only format, resolving ESM/CJS compatibility issues.

## Motivation

Addresses the ESM compatibility issue where `require()` cannot load `.js` files in projects with `"type": "module"`. This was causing the MCP server to fail to find the `language` setting in ESM projects.

## Changes

### Core Changes

#### Config Loader (`config.loader.ts`)
- Removed `loadJsConfig()` function and dynamic `import()` logic
- Removed `isJsConfig()` and `getJsConfigWarning()` helpers
- Simplified `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES` to `['codingbuddy.config.json']` only
- Updated `loadConfigFromFile()` to reject non-JSON formats with clear error message

#### Config Writer (`config.writer.ts`)
- Removed `formatConfigAsJs()` function
- Changed `ConfigFormat` type from `'js' | 'json'` to `'json'`
- Removed `format` option from `WriteConfigOptions`
- Now imports `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES` from config module (DRY compliance)

#### Template Renderers
- `config-renderer.ts`: Removed ~250 lines of JS rendering code
- `template.renderer.ts`: Removed `renderConfigAsJs()` and helper functions
- `templates/index.ts`: Updated exports to remove JS-related functions

#### CLI Updates (`cli.ts`, `cli.types.ts`)
- Removed `--format` CLI option
- Changed default format from `'js'` to `'json'`
- Updated help text to indicate JSON-only support

### Documentation Consistency

## Breaking Changes

### Removed
- Support for `codingbuddy.config.js` files
- Support for `codingbuddy.config.mjs` files
- `--format` CLI option

### Migration Guide

Users with existing JavaScript config files need to convert to JSON:

```bash
# Before (JS)
# codingbuddy.config.js
module.exports = {
  language: 'ko',
  projectName: 'my-app'

author: copilot
body:
Adds a Dark Mode accessibility feature controlled via the Profile Tray, positioned alongside existing accessibility toggles (High Contrast UI, Dyslexia Font).

## Backend
- **Feature Flag**: `dark_mode` in `config/feature_flags/00_standard.yml` (`applies_to: User`, `type: setting`)
- **User Model**: `prefers_dark_mode?` method mirroring `prefers_high_contrast?` pattern
- **Controller**: Exposes preference via `js_env[:prefers_dark_mode]`
- **Layouts**: Apply `dark-mode` class to `<body>` when enabled

## Frontend
- **DarkModeToggle.tsx**: New toggle component following `HighContrastModeToggle` pattern
- **ProfileTray.tsx**: Toggle added under Accessibility Settings section
- **EnvCommon.d.ts**: Added `prefers_dark_mode?: boolean` type

## Dark Theme CSS (`app/stylesheets/base/_dark_mode.scss`)
~2200 lines of color-only overrides. Color palette:

```scss
$dm-bg-darker: #121212;     // Main background
$dm-bg-dark: #1a1a1a;       // Sidebar/nav
$dm-bg-medium: #1e1e1e;     // Cards/panels
$dm-text-primary: #e6e6e6;  // Text
$dm-accent-primary: #4f9cff; // Links/accents
```

Coverage includes: Dashboard, Modules, Assignments, Quizzes, Calendar (including mini calendar), Inbox, Grades, Files, Discussions, People, Settings, Profile Tray, Student View.

## Design Decisions
- No database migration—uses existing FeatureFlag infrastructure
- Only color properties modified (no layout changes)
- PDF previews intentionally remain light for readability
- Student view inherits teacher's dark mode preference when entering student view mode

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## 🔧 Add Dark Mode to Canvas LMS
> 
> **Role:** You are a senior full-stack engineer contributing to the open-source Canvas LMS codebase.  
> Your task is to design and implement a **user-accessible Dark Mode feature** integrated into **Accessibility Settings inside the Profile menu**, with a persistent user preference.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🎯 Goal
> 
> Add a **Dark Mode toggle** to Canvas LMS that:
> 
> 1. Lives in:  
>    **Profile → Settings → Accessibility**
> 2. Saves per-user preference in the database
> 3. Applies a global dark theme across the UI
> 4. Works with existing Canvas theming and React components
> 5. Does not break existing branding/theme overrides
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧩 Part 1 — Backend (Rails)
> 
> **Objective:** Store dark mode as a user preference.
> 
> 1. **Database**
>    - Add a boolean column to the `users` table:
>      ```ruby
>      add_column :users, :prefers_dark_mode, :boolean, default: false, null: false
>      ```
>    - Include migration.
> 
> 2. **Model**
>    - Update `User` model to allow this attribute.
>    - Ensure it's serialized in user settings APIs.
> 
> 3. **API**
>    - Extend the existing user settings endpoint OR create:
>      ```
>      PUT /api/v1/users/:id/preferences
>      ```
>      Body:
>      ```json
>      { "prefers_dark_mode": true }
>      ```
>    - Must require authenticated user and match current user.
> 
> 4. **Serializer**
>    - Expose `prefers_dark_mode` in user JSON payload.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🎨 Part 2 — Frontend Setting UI (React / InstUI)
> 
> **Location:**  
> Profile → Settings → Accessibility panel
> 
> 1. Add a new setting block:
> 
>    **Label:** “Dark Mode”  
>    **Control:** InstUI `Toggle` component  
>    **Description:** “Reduces brightness and uses a dark color theme across Canvas.”
> 
> 2. On toggle:
>    - Update state immediately (optimistic UI)
>    - Persist via API
>    - Add/remove `dark-mode` class on `<body>`
> 
> 3. Load preference on app boot:
>    - Inject value from initial user JSON
>    - Apply theme before full render to prevent flash
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🌙 Part 3 — Theming System
> 
> **Approach:** Use CSS variables, not hard-coded overrides.
> 
> 1. Create global dark theme file:
>    ```
>    app/styles/themes/_dark_mode.scss
>    ```
> 
> 2. Define dark variables:
> 
>    ```scss
>    body.dark-mode {
>      --ic-brand-primary: #4f9cff;
>      --ic-bg-page: #121212;
>      --ic-bg-card: #1e1e1e;
>      --ic-text-dark: #e6e6e6;
>      --ic-text-light: #b3b3b3;
>      --ic-border: #2c2c2c;
>      --ic-link-color: #6ea8ff;
>    }
>    ```
> 
> 3. Ensure:
>    - Uses existing CSS variables where possible
>    - Does NOT break custom institution themes
>    - Keeps contrast AA compliant
> 
> ---
> 
> ### ⚙️ Part 4 — App Initialization
> 
> Modify main layout boot script:
> 
> ```js
> if (ENV.current_user?.prefers_dark_mode) {
>   document.body.classList.add('dark-mode');
> }
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧪 Part 5 — Edge Cases
> 
> Handle:
> 
> - Mobile view
> - High contrast mode compatibility
> - PDF preview pages (should stay light)
> - Email templates (unchanged)
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 📦 Deliverables
> 
> Provide:
> 
> 1. Migration file
> 2. Rails controller updates
> 3. React component code for the toggle
> 4. API call logic
> 5. SCSS dark theme file
> 6. Initialization script changes
> 7. Explanation of how the theme system avoids conflicts
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧠 Engineering Constraints
> 
> - Follow existing Canvas code style
> - Use InstUI components
> - No inline styles
> - No hard-coded colors in components
> - Dark mode must be **purely preference-based**, not system auto-detect
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧭 Outcome
> 
> After implementation, a user should be able to:
> 
> 1. Open Profile → Settings → Accessibility  
> 2. Turn on Dark Mode  
> 3. See the UI switch immediately  
> 4. Reload Canvas and still have Dark Mode enabled


</details>

author: xtermi2
body:
To fix the problem, we need an explicit `getVersion()` method in `FileNameInfoImpl` that is annotated with `@Override` and returns the `version` field. Since Lombok’s `@Getter` cannot be instructed here to add `@Override`, the simplest, behavior-preserving change is to remove `@Getter` from the `version` field and instead define a concrete `getVersion()` method that matches the interface and returns the same field. This preserves functionality while satisfying the rule.

Concretely in `elasticsearch-evolution-core/src/main/java/com/senacor/elasticsearch/evolution/core/internal/model/migration/FileNameInfoImpl.java`:

- Leave the `version` field as a `private final` field, but remove the Lombok `@Getter` annotation from that field.
- Add a public method `MigrationVersion getVersion()` annotated with `@Override` that simply returns `this.version`.
- Do not change the `@Getter` annotations for `description` and `scriptName`, as there is no indication they override interface methods that CodeQL has flagged, and we only change what we must.

No new imports are needed, since `MigrationVersion` is already imported and `@Override` is a standard Java annotation.

body:
The codebase was using the deprecated `DeviceContext` constructor directly instead of the new `DeviceContext.initialize()` factory method introduced in #347.

**Migration pattern:**

```python
# Old (deprecated)
ctx = iris.x.DeviceContext(cur_rank, world_size, heap_bases)

# New
ctx = DeviceContext.initialize(context_tensor, cur_rank, world_size)
```

**Changes:**

- **Kernel signatures**: Replaced `heap_bases: tl.tensor` parameter with `context_tensor`
- **Kernel implementations**: Updated 10 kernels across test files (test_all_to_all, test_all_reduce, test_all_gather, test_reduce_scatter, test_gather)
- **Fused operations**: Updated 4 kernels in iris/ops (all_gather_matmul, matmul_reduce_scatter, matmul_all_gather, matmul_all_reduce)
- **Kernel invocations**: Changed from `shmem.get_heap_bases()` to `shmem.get_device_context()`

The new API encapsulates heap base pointer management within the DeviceContext, following the pattern established in `examples/06_message_passing/message_passing_device_context.py`.

body:
## Summary                                                              
  Fix `PersistedQueryLink` overwriting existing `http` and `fetchOptions` context when calling `setContext()`.

  ## Problem
  `setContext()` was called with an object literal, which completely replaced the existing context. This caused issues when other links or prepareRequest (like `GraphQL17Alpha9Handler` for `@defer` support) had already set context values such as accept headers.

  ## Solution
  Pass a function to `setContext()` that spreads the previous context values before adding new ones, preserving any existing configuration.   

  ## Tests Added
  - `preserves existing http context on initial request`
  - `preserves existing http context on retry`
  - `preserves existing fetchOptions context on retry`

author: angch
body:
This PR adds a memory usage column to the `sentrylogmon --status` command output.

### Why?
Users choose `sentrylogmon` for its lightweight footprint. Exposing the memory usage directly in the status command provides immediate validation of this claim and helps users monitor the health of their logging agents without external tools.

### Changes
- **IPC Protocol:** Added `memory_alloc` field to the JSON response.
- **Server:** Populates this field using `runtime.ReadMemStats`.
- **CLI:**
    - Added `MEM` column to the status table.
    - Renamed `DETAILS` to `MONITORS` for better clarity.
    - Added `formatBytes` helper to show "KiB", "MiB" etc.

### Example Output
```
PID     STARTED              UPTIME   MEM       VERSION   MONITORS
12345   2023-10-27 10:00:00  2d 4h    5.2 MiB   v1.0.0    nginx(file), app(journalctl)
```

### UX Impact
- **Trust:** users see the low footprint.
- **Clarity:** "MONITORS" is more descriptive than "DETAILS".
- **Readability:** Human-readable bytes and clean table alignment.

author: jsmbennett
body:
## Summary
Refactored the context menu animation and positioning logic to use a simpler, more predictable approach based on available horizontal space rather than viewport quadrants.

## Key Changes
- **Simplified animation direction calculation**: Changed from a 4-direction system (animating away from closest corner) to a 2-direction system that defaults to bottom-right and falls back to bottom-left when insufficient space exists on the right side
- **Improved measurement timing**: Moved direction calculation into `requestAnimationFrame` callback to ensure the menu element is visible and measurable before determining its direction
- **Updated documentation**: Clarified the menu behavior in JSDoc comments to reflect the new simpler positioning strategy
- **Code cleanup**: Reorganized animation event listener setup to occur after direction is determined, improving code flow and readability

## Implementation Details
The `_calculateDirection()` method now:
- Takes the menu element as a parameter to measure its width
- Compares available space on the right side (`viewportWidth - x`) against the menu's width
- Returns 'bottom-left' only when necessary, otherwise defaults to 'bottom-right'
- Eliminates unnecessary vertical positioning logic since menus always animate downward

This approach is more intuitive for users and easier to maintain than the previous quadrant-based system.

body:
## What's the reason for this PR?

Inside of the different request performing class, we support:
- async/await & AsyncStream (Swift Concurrency)
- completion handlers
- publishers (Combine)

To prevent writing duplicate code, the completion handler method was used as the CORE implementation, and Swift concurrency and combine methods are wrappers of the completion handler method.

Apple recommends that any new async code should be written in Swift Concurrency.

Follow up to: 
- https://github.com/Aldo10012/EZNetworking/pull/89
- https://github.com/Aldo10012/EZNetworking/pull/90
- https://github.com/Aldo10012/EZNetworking/pull/91

## What's new?

This PR focuses on FileDownloadable. Other classes will be refactored in follow up PRs.

1. Make swift concurrency method the core implementation handling networking logic,
2. Make non swift-concurrency methods be wrapper methods.
3. Replace `.uploadFileTask(...)` return type from `URLSessionUploadTask` to `CancellableRequest`

Potential fix for [https://github.com/bernd3k/obsidian-auto-card-link/security/code-scanning/2](https://github.com/bernd3k/obsidian-auto-card-link/security/code-scanning/2)

In general, to fix this issue you should add a `permissions` block that explicitly limits the `GITHUB_TOKEN` scopes to the minimum required for the workflow or specific job. For a simple lint workflow that only checks out code and installs dependencies, `contents: read` is sufficient, and is the minimal recommended starting point from the warning. This can be specified at the workflow root (applies to all jobs) or under the `lint` job.

The best fix here without changing existing functionality is to add a `permissions` block at the job level for `lint`, since that directly addresses the highlighted job and makes the intent clear. You only need read access to repository contents for checkout; `yarn install` and `yarn lint` do not require write access to the repository via `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Concretely, in `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, add a `permissions:` section under `lint:` (same indentation level as `runs-on:`) with `contents: read`. No imports or additional methods are required, since this is just a YAML configuration change.

This pull request introduces new features for managing certificate backgrounds and teacher signatures, as well as improvements to lesson duration tracking and documentation. It also includes utility scripts for debugging and reporting, and UI enhancements for certificate template management.

**Certificate Background and Signature Management:**

* Added a new `SignatureController` for teachers, allowing them to upload, preview, and delete their signature images and certificate background images, with appropriate validation and storage handling.
* Added a migration and model update to support storing a `certificate_background` image for each user. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-45023d0a74766aee0b24f7dfb57b481b75b719f7ccf3e990e7c749c4c3569d0bR1-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbR29)

**Lesson Duration Tracking:**

* Added a new `required_duration_minutes` field to the `lessons` table (with migration and model update), including validation and default value logic in the lesson creation and update controllers. This tracks the minimum required duration (in minutes) for lesson completion. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7446b4f548b8b8c8753c2b827cc0aea990cc30e7af4c21738b72dae1fb033605R1-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f2735229f7b9e59dee119811b63bc2af1195cc13aceb96e2d9fd2525e2c5965cR19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bb8cf1e6871832d67b5e90749e836eb972ca59547fb43d56b325d510651258e9R66-R73) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-bb8cf1e6871832d67b5e90749e836eb972ca59547fb43d56b325d510651258e9R174-R181)

**Certificate Template UI Improvements:**

* Enhanced the admin certificate template create/edit forms to allow uploading a background image for certificates, with user guidance and error handling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-94c00d988e149a3b9989a27134cd097aa7b36254953a54a378fe12c4e2ef60f3R52-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4f462431f1b55c060c032f750c233fdd0dd409fef3570f69e94c69b610823850R51-R82)

**Documentation and Utility Scripts:**

* Renamed and expanded the main documentation index, adding more detailed project statistics and links to new key documents. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f96acdcfd14905e793eb9a1e83848cf214a4e037470d0cb842c403903b50dc08R2-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f96acdcfd14905e793eb9a1e83848cf214a4e037470d0cb842c403903b50dc08L12-R31)

## Summary
Testing the updated heads_up category implementation where it's now a proper category but used as a fallback for cross-cutting patterns.

## Cross-Cutting Patterns Added

### cross_cutting_patterns.py
- **Global caching**: Spans security (cache poisoning), performance (optimization), maintainability (memory management)
- **Input sanitization**: Security (protection), readability (consistency), business logic (requirements)
- **Retry with backoff**: Performance (reliability), UX (error handling), maintainability (complexity)
- **Config validation with defaults**: Security (safe defaults), development (convenience), maintainability (robustness)

### kishkush.js
- **Data processing pipeline**: Security (input validation), performance (length limits), maintainability (type handling)
- **Error handling patterns**: UX (user feedback), security (information leaks), maintainability (debugging)

## Expected Behavior
With the updated heads_up category as a proper category but emphasized as fallback, these patterns should trigger heads_up classification when the AI cannot determine a single primary category.

- Updated `@isaacs/brace-expansion` 5.0.0 → 5.0.1 in `package-lock.json`

body:
## Summary
This PR fixes multiple CSS syntax errors in inline styles and adds null safety checks throughout the codebase to prevent runtime errors when optional data is missing.

## Key Changes

### CSS Syntax Fixes
- Fixed incomplete `rgba()` color values by adding missing color components:
  - `rgba(184;` → `rgba(184, 134, 11, 0.08)` (dark gold with transparency)
  - `rgba(0;` → `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` (black overlay)
- Fixed incomplete `linear-gradient()` declarations by adding missing color stops:
  - `linear-gradient(135deg;` → `linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(184, 134, 11, 0.1), rgba(184, 134, 11, 0.05))`

### Null Safety Improvements
- Added null checks for optional data structures:
  - `VersionCard` component now returns `null` if version data is missing
  - Conditional rendering for `aoBreakdown`, `keyStrengths`, `keyWeaknesses`, and `overallComment`
  - Added checks before accessing `comparison.remainingTargets`
  - Added checks for `initialVersion`, `improvedVersion`, and `comparison` before rendering sections
- Fixed potential undefined access with `version.percentage != null ? \`${version.percentage}%\` : ''`

### Report Generation Logic
- Refactored report building to conditionally include sections based on available data
- Wrapped improvement summary, initial version, and final version sections in conditional blocks
- Added proper string concatenation with template literals for better readability

### Data Tracking
- Added `originalEssay` and `essaysAreDifferent` fields to submission data to track whether essays were modified
- Improved paragraph data mapping to preserve original text before corrections

## Notable Implementation Details
- All CSS fixes maintain the existing design intent with proper color values (dark gold theme)
- Null checks prevent rendering empty sections while maintaining layout integrity
- Report generation now gracefully handles missing optional assessment data

author: rudi77
body:
### Motivation
- Remove the `profile` field from client-facing execution/integration request schemas and centralize which infra profile is used internally to reduce client surface area and ambiguity.
- Allow `sub_agent` tool specs to be declared minimally with `name` and use that `name` as the canonical identifier (fallback to `specialist` when omitted) to reduce duplication in multi-agent profiles.
- Provide a ready multi-agent coding workflow (planner/worker/reviewer) and corresponding configs so the orchestrator can delegate work via sub-agent tools.

### Description
- Removed `profile` properties from `ExecuteMissionRequest` and `InboundMessageRequest` Pydantic models and made the API pass the internal default profile (`"dev"`) into `AgentExecutor`/`CommunicationOptions` instead of relying on a client-supplied value.
- Updated API docs and examples in `docs/api.md` and supporting docs to stop sending `profile` in requests and to prefer `agent_id` when selecting an agent definition.
- Added a new `SubAgentTool` implementation (`src/taskforce/infrastructure/tools/orchestration/sub_agent_tool.py`) and wired `AgentFactory._instantiate_tool` to detect `type: sub_agent` dicts and instantiate them via a new `_instantiate_sub_agent_tool` helper that accepts `name` and falls back `specialist = tool_spec.get('specialist') or name`.
- Added/updated orchestration/profile configs including `src/taskforce_extensions/configs/coding_agent.yaml` and three custom sub-agent configs under `configs/custom/` (`coding_planner.yaml`, `coding_worker.yaml`, `coding_reviewer.yaml`) and documented the sub-agent usage in `docs/profiles.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed locally for this change; CI is expected to run the full test suite (`uv run pytest`) on push.

author: simensrostad
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the power module's initialization and state management, particularly around modem initialization. The main changes include introducing a wait state for modem initialization, refactoring ZBus channel usage for internal messaging, and updating the test suite to accommodate these changes.

**Power module initialization and state management:**

- Added a new state (`STATE_WAITING_FOR_MODEM_INIT`) to the power module's state machine, ensuring the module waits for the modem to initialize before transitioning to the running state. This is handled via a private ZBus channel and a modem initialization callback (`on_modem_init`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4abd9b2c4df4069dc539d9d3d62b78426937f3d7b63b499b9e199853eb9d5778R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4abd9b2c4df4069dc539d9d3d62b78426937f3d7b63b499b9e199853eb9d5778L41-R74) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4abd9b2c4df4069dc539d9d3d62b78426937f3d7b63b499b9e199853eb9d5778R101-R133) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4abd9b2c4df4069dc539d9d3d62b78426937f3d7b63b499b9e199853eb9d5778L90-R194) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4abd9b2c4df4069dc539d9d3d62b78426937f3d7b63b499b9e199853eb9d5778L483-R569)
- Refactored ZBus channel definitions by introducing a private channel (`PRIV_POWER_CHAN`) for internal state management and using macros to manage observers and message sizes more cleanly.

**Testing and configuration updates:**

- Updated the power module test suite to simulate modem initialization via the new callback mechanism and verify correct initialization sequencing. Added a new test to check module initialization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-72444b0baa12cf258fa72207203ceff2ac5865d49a3d2e7bbfdc6533e6d21f22R23-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-72444b0baa12cf258fa72207203ceff2ac5865d49a3d2e7bbfdc6533e6d21f22R121-R129)

**Configuration cleanup:**

- Removed redundant Memfault logging buffer configuration from `app/prj.conf` and adjusted the buffer size in `app/overlay-memfault.conf` for consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb291163c60fa4840263907846afa131206d351a5248ce4085cc41af48f243dfL10-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-44c49245e3507ea76cafeca22e652e4f30a24495a147d0beb5681a7bad5b0b71L203-L205)

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/bernd3k/obsidian-auto-card-link/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/bernd3k/obsidian-auto-card-link/security/code-scanning/1)

In general, the fix is to explicitly declare `permissions` for the workflow or for the job, narrowing `GITHUB_TOKEN` to only what is required. This workflow creates a release and uploads release assets, which GitHub authorizes via the `contents` permission. Therefore, the minimal appropriate permission is `contents: write`. Declaring this at the job level suffices, but you can also put it at the workflow root if all jobs share the same needs; here there is a single `build` job, so either is fine.

The best minimal change without altering functionality is to add a `permissions` block under the `build` job (line 12), between `build:` and `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. This will scope the `GITHUB_TOKEN` for that job to `contents: write`, which is required for `actions/create-release` and `actions/upload-release-asset` to work, and avoids implicitly granting broader, unused privileges (such as `issues`, `pull-requests`, etc.). No additional imports, methods, or other definitions are needed: it is purely a YAML configuration change in `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

body:
#### Summary Content "Multilevel Exodii dungeon in the string dimension" #### Purpose of change Adding more content to the "string" dimension #### Describe the solution This adds a globally unique, 3x3x4 dungeon to the string dimension. It can only spawn in the "scars," which are the recently implemented rocky fields. It is a failed or abandoned Exodii node (it's unclear which). Something happened, and the true exodii are gone. All remaining "denizens" are presumably non-citizens cyborgs, now long dead (i.e., now zomborgs). Given that the first visits to the dimension are very short, and only get longer with time, the player will have to visit several times to have a hope of finding and doing the dungeon. They'll also have to bring supplies, and then perhaps make some tough decisions about what to bring back, since whatever they bring has to come on their back. The bottom layer, which presumably had housing, power generation, portal tech, etc., is mostly gone - sundered by whatever sundered this world. It's unknown if it happened before or after they left. In its place is a distorted maze infected with strangling string nether creatures and hounds of tindalos. The ground level is what the player finds. It looks like a large, circular fortress of scrap metal and concrete. The doors are locked, and there are turret-boxes/towers around with broken turrets inside. Inside (if the player can get in) is a level with what used to be artificial gardens, now dead and frozen from lack of power. Lots of frostbitten zomborgs wander around. The upper level is their former trading floor. It has a few small warehouses with exodii goods, and a modest, locked bionic vault. It has a few frostbitten zomborg devourers, and one zomborg boss that is more heavily armored. The boss has a physical key the vault. There's also a roof, with not much on it. There are several ways to break in (spoilers):
- The "intended" way is to descend some z-level strings that obliterated the south-west tower, leading into the warped basement. Then the player will need to navigate the maze to reach the only remaining stairs, to the far north-east tower. You can then climb into the upper level and combat/loot. Navigating the maze can take several paths - either one way through tons of strangling string monsters, or a way with fewer string monsters, but with hounds of tindalos (and some remaining corners for them to warp to). The layout is more or less the same every time, but the pathway can be broken by random voids, and doors can be randomly locked, so the "best" path shifts between playthroughs. - The player can break down the metal doors, if they somehow brought tools to do so from their home dimension. They'll have to fight through a lot of zomborgs, though. - An astute player can climb the Z-strings to the roof level and jump to the roof, and then climb down. However, they'll have to be light/skilled enough to jump, which may limit their combat ability. Then there's getting back down. Falling and getting injured in another dimension isn't very wise. - Presumably several others I haven't thought of. -
Screenshots: - Typical overmap spawn:
- z -1:
- z 0:
- z +1:
- z +2:
#### Describe alternatives you've considered Having it be a "local" structure, instead of Exodii. Having Exodii be there. #### Testing Went to dimension, looked for special. #### Additional context I think more can be done with this: local kipple & trade goods on the shelves, maybe Exodii tech from other dimensions, maybe a dead/zombified exodii, maybe a way to let the player know this place exists. Will follow up in future PRs.

- **server.js**: Updated Authorization header from `token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}` to `Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}` for GitHub API requests

The `token` prefix was deprecated by GitHub in favor of `Bearer` for Personal Access Token authentication.

```diff
  headers: {
-   Authorization: `token ${GITHUB_TOKEN}`,
+   Authorization: `Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}`,
    Accept: 'application/vnd.github.v3+json',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  }
```

body: # Pull Request ## Description Added property-based tests using `fast-check` to `packages/sdk/src/__tests__/serialization.test.ts`. These tests verify the round-trip integrity of Borsh serialization, ensuring that `serialize(deserialize(x)) == x` for various data types and structures. This enhances the robustness of the serialization logic by testing against a wide range of randomly generated valid inputs. ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Code refactoring ## Related Issues ## Checklist - [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes - [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published ## Testing ### Unit Tests ```bash pnpm test ``` All existing and newly added property-based tests pass. author: sphereisaiahmin-dev
body:
### Motivation
- The reverse toggle reset playback to the beginning and only worked when a timeline dot was clicked, which broke expected pause/reverse/resume behavior.
- The desired behavior is to allow reversing while paused or playing, preserve the current offset when pausing, start reversing immediately when playing, and begin reversing on next play when toggled while paused.

### Description
- Updated `nowPos()` to return a stable offset when `isPlaying` is false and to safeguard against `player.buffer` being undefined by returning `0` in that case.
- When pausing via the play button the code now saves the current position by setting `offset = nowPos()` before calling `player.stop()` so the position is preserved for later resume or reverse operations.
- Changed `reverseBtn.onclick` to permit toggling reverse while paused by checking `player.buffer.loaded`, computing `wasPlaying = isPlaying`, toggling `player.reverse`, stopping and updating `offset`, and only restarting playback (and the loop checker) if `wasPlaying` was true.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent duplicate panorama markers and lingering click handlers when the panorama list or view mode changes.
- Ensure marker click interactions are correctly rebound and removed to avoid multiple event triggers and potential memory leaks.

### Description
- Clear the panorama `markerGroup` before re-adding markers by calling `group.clear()` to avoid duplicates.
- Change `setupMarkerInteraction` to register a named `handleClick` and return a removal function that detaches the click listener from the DOM element.
- Capture the removal function in the effect and call it on cleanup, so click handlers are removed when markers or view state change.
- Update the effect dependencies to include `viewMode` and `setSelectedPano` so interactions are rebound when view mode changes.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.
- The change was committed after local code edits and no CI or type-check runs were executed as part of this rollout.

body:
### Problem description
The `tt-forge-models` repository currently uses multiple directory layouts depending on
the framework and number of tasks:

- JAX models follow: `model_name / task / framework / model_code`
- PyTorch models with a single task follow: `model_name / framework / model_code`
- PyTorch models with multiple tasks follow: `model_name / task / framework / model_code`

With plans to add ONNX and Paddle models, maintaining multiple layout conventions
introduces inconsistency, increases maintenance overhead, and complicates automation
and tooling.

the new structure is :
```
└── <model_name>
    └── <task>           
        └── <framework> 
                └── init.py
                    loader.py
```

eg: for alexnet model 

```
└── <alexnet>
    └── <image_classification>           
        └── <pytorch> 
                └── init.py
                    loader.py
```
### What's changed
All models are now standardized to a single unified directory structure


I have attached the logs for your reference:
[collect_all_models.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24407336/collect_all_models.log)

I have verified the changes by making sure the tests that changed are getting collected

author: cskiro
body:
## Chapter: Eliminating the Plugin Manifest War

### The Ask
After upgrading to latest Claude Code, `/doctor` reported 24 plugin errors:
- 23 "Plugin has conflicting manifests" errors
- 1 "Hook load failed" error for cc-insights

### The Journey
1. **Root cause analysis**: Claude Code was finding both marketplace.json entries AND individual plugin.json files, causing manifest conflicts
2. **First fix**: Deleted all 23 plugin.json files - metadata now lives exclusively in marketplace.json (single source of truth)
3. **Second fix**: cc-insights hooks.json used wrong schema format. Anthropic's hook schema requires nested matcher-groups with `hooks` arrays, not direct handlers
4. **Verification**: Reinstalled marketplace, ran `/doctor` - 0 errors

### The Architecture

**Before (broken)**:
```
marketplace.json → defines plugin metadata
plugin.json → ALSO defines plugin metadata
Claude Code → "conflicting manifests!"
```

**After (fixed)**:
```
marketplace.json → single source of truth
skills/ directory → auto-discovered by Claude Code
hooks/ directory → auto-discovered by Claude Code
```

**Hook schema fix**:
```json
// WRONG (old format)
{ "hooks": { "Stop": [{ "command": ["bash", "./path"] }] }}

// CORRECT (Anthropic format)
{ "hooks": { "Stop": [{ "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/path" }] }] }}
```

### The Outcome
- 23 plugin.json files deleted
- cc-insights hooks.json converted to correct schema
- `/doctor` shows 0 plugin errors
- All 23 plugins load successfully

### The Lessons
- Anthropic's hook schema uses **matcher groups** containing **hooks arrays** - not direct handlers
- Use `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for paths in hooks, not relative `./` paths
- Single source of truth for plugin metadata prevents conflicts

### Commit Narrative
- `fix(marketplace)`: Single commit addressing both manifest conflicts and hook schema

### References
- [Anthropic Hook Documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- [Official hookify plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/hookify)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview
Design and build a modern, animated startup landing website with a mechanical/manufacturing industry aesthetic. The website should showcase services, sell courses, accept custom orders, and build trust through professional design and smooth animations.

## Theme & Style Requirements

### Visual Identity
- **Color Palette**: Blue and white (clean, professional, industrial look)
- **Typography**: Classic old book/serif style (similar to traditional printed books like Merriweather, Playfair Display, or Libre Baskerville)
- **Industry Feel**: Strong mechanical/manufacturing company aesthetic
- **Imagery**: High-quality component, machinery, and industrial photos throughout
- **Animations**: Smooth, professional animations using GSAP
- **Responsive**: Fully responsive design for desktop and mobile devices

## Website Structure & Sections

### 1. Hero Section
- Simple, strong heading describing the startup's mission in manufacturing and services
- Short clarifying subheading
- Two prominent CTA buttons:
  - "Explore Services"
  - "View Courses"
- GSAP fade and slide-in animations on page load

### 2. Services Section
- Display all manufacturing and service offerings in a card layout
- Each card includes:
  - Icon representing the service
  - Service title
  - Short description
- Scroll-triggered GSAP animations for each service card (stagger effect)

### 3. About Us Section
- Comprehensive explanation of the company and its offerings
- Button to download/view company brochure (PDF placeholder)
- Smooth text reveal animation using GSAP

### 4. Courses Section (Highlighted)
- **Important**: Dedicated section showcasing educational courses being sold
- Course cards displaying:
  - Course name
  - Short benefit description
  - "Enroll" button/CTA
- Must be accessible from top navigation bar
- GSAP fade + scale animations on scroll

### 5. Order Requirements Section (NEW - Critical Feature)
- Dedicated form section for customers to submit custom order details
- Form fields required:
  - Company name
  - Product name
  - Product description
  - Product measurements/specifications
  - Customer credentials/contact information
  - Additional order requirements (textarea)
- Clean, professional form design
- Smooth animations on input focus and form submission
- Form validation

### 6. Contact & Reviews Section
- **Contact Form** with fields:
  - Name
  - Email
  - Message
- Display company email address prominently
- **Reviews/Testimonials Area**:
  - 2-3 sample reviews to build trust
  - Clean card-based layout
- Smooth slide and fade animations

### 7. Footer Section
- Company information and branding
- Navigation links (Services, About, Courses, Order Requirements, Contact)
- Social media icon placeholders (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, Instagram)
- Copyright information

## Technical Requirements

### Technology Stack
- **Frontend Framework**: React (latest version)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
- **Animations**: GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform)
- **Icons**: React Icons or similar library

### Performance & Quality
- Clean, modular component architecture
- Optimized GSAP animations (no performance issues)
- Fast loading times
- Lazy loading for images where appropriate
- SEO-friendly structure

### Design Principles
- Strong mechanical/industrial branding throughout
- Use industrial component imagery and layouts that look realistic
- Professional color scheme (blues and whites)
- Clear visual hierarchy
- Excellent spacing and typography
- Smooth scroll behavior

### Future Expandability
The codebase should be structured to easily accommodate:
- User authentication/login system
- Payment integration for courses
- Admin dashboard
- CMS integration
- Database connectivity for forms

## Deliverables

1. **Complete React Application** with:
   - `package.json` with all dependencies
   - Proper project structure
   - All components modularized

2. **All Sections Implemented**:
   - Hero with animations
   - Services showcase
   - About Us with brochure download
   - Courses section (accessible via nav)
   - Order Requirements form
   - Contact & Reviews
   - Footer

3. **GSAP Animations**:
   - Hero entrance animations
   - Scroll-triggered animations for services
   - Smooth transitions throughout
   - Form interaction animations

4. **Responsive Design**:
   - Mobile-first approach
   - Tablet and desktop breakpoints
   - Touch-friendly interactions

5. **Assets**:
   - Placeholder images for industrial/mechanical components
   - Icon set for services
   - Sample review content

## Example Content Suggestions

### Sample Services
- CNC Machining
- Metal Fabrication
- Welding Services
- Quality Inspection
- Custom Manufacturing
- Assembly Services

### Sample Courses
- "Introduction to CNC Programming"
- "Welding Fundamentals"
- "Quality Control in Manufacturing"
- "Industrial Safety Certification"

### Sample Reviews
- Client testimonial about service quality
- Feedback on course effectiveness
- Comments on ...

### Motivation
- Permettre d'uploader et mettre à jour une image utilisée en arrière-plan de la section hero de la page d'accueil.

### Description
- Ajout de la clé `hero_image_path` dans `HomePage::$fillable` et dans les valeurs par défaut retournées par `HomePage::defaultData()`.
- Ajout d'une migration `database/migrations/2024_10_20_000002_add_hero_image_path_to_home_pages_table.php` qui ajoute la colonne `hero_image_path` nullable à la table `home_pages`.
- Gestion de l'upload dans `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\HomeController::update()` : validation du fichier `hero_image`, suppression du fichier précédent via `Storage::disk('public')->delete(...)` et stockage du nouveau fichier dans `home/hero` sur le disque `public` (champ enregistré en `hero_image_path`).
- Mise à jour des vues : le formulaire admin (`resources/views/admin/home/edit.blade.php`) accepte désormais `enctype="multipart/form-data"`, affiche un aperçu si l'image existe et propose un champ `type="file"`; la vue publique (`resources/views/accueil.blade.php`) utilise l'image stockée via `Storage::url(...)` comme background CSS avec une image de secours.

### Testing
- Tentative de démarrer le serveur avec `php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8000` a échoué à cause d'un environnement non initialisé (`vendor/autoload.php` manquant), donc l'application n'a pas été démarrée ni les migrations appliquées.
- Aucune suite de tests automatisés n'a été exécutée en raison de l'environnement non bootstrappé.

author: jamesfconway
body:
### Motivation
- The `panel` rule's `replacement` function and surrounding `addRule` call were missing closing braces, causing subsequent rules to be nested incorrectly and preventing proper parsing.

### Description
- Added the missing `}` to close the `replacement` function and `});` to close the `service.addRule("panel", {...})` call immediately after the `return "\n\n" + lines.join("\n") + "\n\n";` line in `converter.js`.
- This restores the intended rule boundary so `mentionPlaceholder` and other rules are defined at the correct scope.

### Testing
- Executed `node -e "require('./converter.js')"`, which fails in Node due to `window` being undefined in this browser-targeted module and is expected to fail in this environment. (failed)
- Executed `node -e "const fs=require('fs'); new Function(fs.readFileSync('converter.js','utf8')); console.log('ok');"` to validate the file parses as valid JavaScript, which printed `ok`. (succeeded)
- Verified `converter.js` loads without syntax errors and that the `mentionPlaceholder` rule is now registered after the `panel` rule by inspecting the file structure. (succeeded)

author: juliaregistrator
body:
- Registering package: MultiFloats
- Repository: https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl
- Created by: @dzhang314
- Version: v3.0.0
- Commit: 173f83849bed47428595215a863f859268416970
- Reviewed by: @dzhang314
- Reference: https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/commit/173f83849bed47428595215a863f859268416970#commitcomment-176385068
- Description: Fast, SIMD-accelerated extended-precision arithmetic for Julia
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
**MultiFloats.jl v3.0** introduces new arithmetic algorithms that are **simultaneously faster and more accurate** than **MultiFloats.jl v2.0** (and, to my knowledge, all other multiprecision libraries). These new algorithms always return results in normalized form, solving the [denormalization issues](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/issues/42) that caused [spurious accuracy losses](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/issues/45) in **MultiFloats.jl v2.0**.

**MultiFloats.jl v3.0** also introduces a round-trip-safe float-to-string conversion algorithm, guaranteeing that conversion of a `MultiFloat` to string and back always yields a numerically identical result.

**MultiFloats.jl v3.0** exports the types `Float32x2`, `Float32x3`, and `Float32x4`, which are intended for use on processors lacking `Float64` hardware support (e.g., GPUs and NPUs). Note that `Float64x2` is faster and slightly more accurate than `Float32x4`; it should be preferred on hardware with native `Float64` support.

Other notable changes:

- The new multiplication algorithm strictly obeys the commutative law. Previously, it was possible for `x * y` to be [slightly different](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/issues/50) from `y * x` due to internal accumulation of floating-point rounding errors.
- Comparison operators (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`) are now significantly faster because it is no longer necessary to run a renormalization loop on their inputs.
- The formula for `precision(MultiFloat{T,N})` has been slightly changed to better reflect the known error bounds for the new arithmetic algorithms.
- `rand(Float32xN)` has been implemented.
- `Base.decompose` has been implemented, which enables [hashing](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/pull/55) and [comparison to rational numbers](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/issues/54).
- Significant correctness issues have been fixed in `prevfloat` and `nextfloat`. Previously, it was possible for these functions to skip over intermediate values because they did not properly consider interactions between multiple limbs.
- A new function, `MultiFloats.canonize`, has been added to convert all numerically equivalent `MultiFloat` values to a single canonical representation. Previously, `MultiFloats.renormalize` was thought to be sufficient, but in extremely rare (roughly 1 in 2^53) cases, it is possible for a single number to have multiple distinct normalized representations.
- Two new functions, `MultiFloats.isnormalized` and `MultiFloats.iscanonical`, have been added to determine whether a `MultiFloat` is in normalized or canonical form, respectively. These are almost always synonymous, but in extremely rare (roughly 1 in 2^53) cases, it is possible for a `MultiFloat` to be normalized but not canonical.

## Breaking Changes from v2.0

The types `Float64x5`, `Float64x6`, `Float64x7`, and `Float64x8` have been removed from the initial release of **MultiFloats.jl v3.0**. The arithmetic algorithms for these types were [fundamentally broken in **MultiFloats.jl v2.0**](https://github.com/dzhang314/MultiFloats.jl/issues/42), and new algorithms that are provably correct for all possible inputs have not yet been found. Computer searches for correct algorithms are ongoing, and these types will be reinstated once such algorithms are found.

The SIMD vector types have been renamed from `v8Float64x2` to `Vec8Float64x2` to follow Julia's convention of capitalizing type names.
`````
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/compare/v2.3.5...v2.4.0)

### NumPy 2.4.0 Release Notes

The NumPy 2.4.0 release continues the work to improve free threaded Python
support, user dtypes implementation, and annotations. There are many expired
deprecations and bug fixes as well.

This release supports Python versions 3.11-3.14

#### Highlights

Apart from annotations and `same_value` kwarg, the 2.4 highlights are mostly
of interest to downstream developers. They should help in implementing new user
dtypes.

- Many annotation improvements. In particular, runtime signature introspection.
- New `casting` kwarg `'same_value'` for casting by value.
- New `PyUFunc_AddLoopsFromSpec` function that can be used to add user sort
  loops using the `ArrayMethod` API.
- New `__numpy_dtype__` protocol.

#### Deprecations

##### Setting the `strides` attribute is deprecated

Setting the strides attribute is now deprecated since mutating
an array is unsafe if an array is shared, especially by multiple
threads. As an alternative, you can create a new view (no copy) via:

- `np.lib.stride_tricks.strided_window_view` if applicable,
- `np.lib.stride_tricks.as_strided` for the general case,
- or the `np.ndarray` constructor (`buffer` is the original array) for a
  light-weight version.

([gh-28925](https://redirect.github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/28925))

##### Positional `out` argument to `np.maximum`, `np.minimum` is deprecated

Passing the output array `out` positionally to `numpy.maximum` and
`numpy.minimum` is deprecated. For example, `np.maximum(a, b, c)` will emit
a deprecation warning, since `c` is treated as the output buffer rather than
a third input.

Always pass the output with the keyword form, e.g. `np.maximum(a, b, out=c)`.

body:
## Summary

- Add complete backtesting system that replays historical data through the LLM anomaly detection pipeline, simulates trade execution, and computes performance metrics
- Implement three-layer architecture: shared types (Zod schemas + IPC contract), agent layer (BacktestExecutor, MetricsCalculator, BacktestEngine orchestrator), and Rust backend (SQLite persistence + Tauri commands)
- Build full frontend with config form (symbols, dates, risk limits, detection thresholds), progress bar, results dashboard (equity curve SVG, trade table, monthly heatmap, per-symbol breakdown), and JSON/CSV export

## Changes

**Shared types** (`shared/src/backtest.ts`): BacktestConfig, BacktestProgress, BacktestTrade, BacktestMetrics, BacktestResult schemas with Zod validation. IPC commands (start, cancel, list, get, delete, export) and events (progress, complete).

**Agent layer** (`agent/src/backtesting/`):
- `BacktestExecutor` — simulated order executor with FIFO lot tracking, cash management, portfolio snapshots
- `MetricsCalculator` — computes Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown, win rate, profit factor, consecutive wins/losses, monthly returns, per-symbol breakdown
- `BacktestEngine` — orchestrates full replay: fetches data, groups by date, runs analysis, filters by severity/confidence, generates trades through risk manager, emits progress events

**Rust backend** (`src-tauri/src/`):
- Migration 003: `backtests` and `backtest_trades` tables with indexes
- Serde types: `BacktestConfig`, `BacktestSummary`, `BacktestTrade`
- Tauri commands: `backtest_start`, `backtest_list`, `backtest_get`, `backtest_get_trades`, `backtest_delete`

**Frontend** (`src/`):
- `BacktestConfig` page — full config form with data selection, portfolio settings, risk limits, detection thresholds, progress bar, recent runs list
- `BacktestResults` page — summary metric cards, SVG equity curve with drawdown shading and trade markers, sortable trade table, monthly returns heatmap, collapsible per-symbol breakdown, JSON/CSV export
- Zustand `backtest-slice` for state management
- Sidebar nav item and App.tsx routing with config/results view toggle

## Test plan

- [x] 626/626 TypeScript tests pass (vitest)
- [x] BacktestExecutor: buy/sell execution, FIFO lots, partial sells, rejection cases, portfolio snapshots (7 tests)
- [x] MetricsCalculator: empty trades, total return, win rate, drawdown, profit factor, consecutive streaks, per-symbol, monthly returns, Sharpe ratio (8 tests)
- [x] BacktestEngine: construction, full run with mocks, cancellation, error handling (4 tests)
- [x] Backtest slice: initial state, setters, add/remove runs, comparison IDs (7 tests)
- [x] Shared schemas: config validation, rejection of invalid timeframes/empty symbols, progress/trade/metrics/result validation (8 tests)
- [ ] Manual: run `pnpm dev`, navigate to Backtest tab, configure and start a backtest, verify progress updates and results display

### Motivation
- Harden control-flow flattening and make the obfuscation pipeline more tolerant to partial failures when transforming real assemblies.
- Reduce runtime/logging noise and avoid null-reference and threading issues during name/random generation and assembly manipulation.

### Description
- Add a new `ControlFlowFlattener` (`Obfuscator/ControlFlow/ControlFlowFlattener.cs`) and wire it into the pipeline by adding it to the project and calling it from `Obfuscate.Execute` via the new `ExecuteStep` wrapper.
- Make the flattener more defensive by guarding `Execute` with a `try/catch`, improving block splitting to handle `Switch` targets and block terminators, adding `IsBlockTerminator`, and using `TryGetTargetIndex`/`TryGetFallThroughIndex` helpers when rewriting branches.
- Introduce step-level error handling in `Obfuscate` by wrapping each pass in `ExecuteStep(string, Action)` and guarding against a `null` `module` parameter.
- Improve `ClassRandomization` and `Randomize` robustness by adding `module`/`assembly` null checks, replacing `Console.WriteLine` with `Debug.WriteLine`, and making the random string generator thread-safe with a locked static `Random` instance.

### Testing

body:
### Motivation
- Make the 2D/overhead table mapping precisely match the photographed cushion and pocket geometry so the visual mapping lines align with actual cushion cuts and jaws.
- Prevent balls from escaping the playfield by treating the mapped cushion/jaw outlines as authoritative field borders during physics updates.

### Description
- Set `POCKET_JAW_MAPPING_RADIUS_SCALE` to `1` to align the jaw mapping arc with the true pocket radius so mapping lines match cushion cuts (`PoolRoyale.jsx`).
- Introduce `TABLE_FIELD_BOUNDS` and derive it from computed cushion/jaw `CUSHION_SEGMENTS` by adding `getFieldBoundsFromSegments(...)` and storing the result in `updateCushionSegmentsFromTable(...)` (`PoolRoyale.jsx`).
- Add `clampBallToField(ball)` which uses the derived bounds (with a small guard and pocket-capture exceptions) to keep balls inside the field and damp/reflect velocity when clamped (`PoolRoyale.jsx`).
- Call `clampBallToField(b)` during the per-ball physics loop right after rail/jaw collision handling so the clamp runs as part of the physics step (`PoolRoyale.jsx`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change; runtime validation is recommended in the client (play a few shots including near-pocket and high-power shots) to confirm mapping alignment and that balls no longer escape the table.

### Motivation
- Complete missing card detail fields so the Card Detail UI shows full content for Major and Wands decks across all locales. 
- Keep existing IDs, titles, keywords and asset paths intact and follow the repo's per-locale JSON data pattern.

### Description
- Added `meaning.detailed`, `funFact`, and `stats` (luck/power/love/clarity) to all Major (22) and Wands (14) cards in the per-locale data files `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_en.json`, `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_ru.json`, and `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_kk.json` without changing existing IDs, titles, keywords or ordering. (36 cards updated per locale.)
- Preserved existing `meaning` structure (`general`, `light`, `shadow`, `advice`) and only extended it with `detailed` entries where missing.
- Added a small validation script at `app_flutter/scripts/validate_cards.js` that checks each `major_` and `wands_` card in `cards_en.json`, `cards_ru.json`, and `cards_kk.json` has `keywords`, `meaning.general`, `meaning.detailed`, `funFact`, and integer `stats` fields (`luck`, `power`, `love`, `clarity`).

### Testing
- Ran the new validator with `node app_flutter/scripts/validate_cards.js` and it printed success: `All major and wands cards have required fields for en/ru/kk.` (exit code 0).
- Verified counts per locale with a quick script: each of `cards_en.json`, `cards_ru.json`, and `cards_kk.json` contains 36 updated cards that start with `major_` or `wands_` (22 major + 14 wands).

Modified files:
- `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_en.json`
- `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_ru.json`
- `app_flutter/assets/data/cards_kk.json`
- `app_flutter/scripts/validate_cards.js`

How to run the validator:
- From repo root run: `node app_flutter/scripts/validate_cards.js`
